systems.name: The Bethesda System – Anal cytology
systems.specimen: Anal canal brushings/swabs (LBC preferred)
use: Anal cancer screening in high-risk groups: people living with HIV (esp. MSM), transplant recipients, women with vulvar/cervical HPV disease (IANS 2024 consensus).
not_use: Rectal mucosal lesions (endoscopy/biopsy).
Perianal skin lesions (biopsy).
report_structure: Adequacy (with transformation zone component: rectal columnar/metaplastic cells)
Interpretation (same squamous terminology as cervical TBS)

adequacy.title: Adequacy (LBC)
items: ≈2,000–3,000 nucleated squamous cells; ThinPrep ≈1–2 nucleated squamous cells/HPF, SurePath ≈3–6/HPF (Bethesda criteria; as summarised in ‘Anal-Rectal Cytology: The Other Pap Test’, Lab Medicine, doi 10.1309/LMHYS464MYWZOXFW).
Transformation zone component: rectal columnar or squamous metaplastic cells – reported, not required.
Conventional smears are less reliable (faecal contamination, air drying).

categories.name: Unsatisfactory for evaluation
categories.definition: Insufficient nucleated squamous cells or obscuring material.

rom.source: TBS 2014

categories.management: Repeat anal cytology (consider avoiding lubricant/enema prior).
criteria: LBC: fewer than ~2,000–3,000 nucleated squamous cells (≈1–2 cells/HPF on ThinPrep; ≈3–6 cells/HPF on SurePath).
>75% obscured by faecal material, bacteria, blood.
Anucleate squames do not count.

diagnoses.name: Unsatisfactory – scant nucleated squamous cells
diagnoses.final: Specimen adequacy: Unsatisfactory for evaluation – insufficient nucleated squamous cells.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat anal cytology recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Specimen adequacy: Unsatisfactory

diagnoses.name: Unsatisfactory – obscuring faecal material
diagnoses.final: Specimen adequacy: Unsatisfactory – obscured by faecal material/bacteria.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat sampling recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Specimen adequacy: Unsatisfactory

categories.name: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
categories.definition: No squamous intraepithelial lesion; organisms may be reported.

rom.source: Systematic review & meta-analysis of anal cytology, risk of AIN2+ (PMC9588562)

categories.management: Routine screening interval per risk group.
criteria: Anucleate and nucleated squames, rectal columnar cells and/or metaplastic cells (transformation zone component reported).
Organisms: Candida, HSV, Enterobius ova, amoebae, faecal bacteria are normal flora.

diagnoses.name: NILM
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Anal transformation zone component present/absent.
diagnoses.comment: Routine follow-up per screening protocol.
diagnoses.cat: Interpretation: NILM (Bethesda terminology, anal cytology)

diagnoses.name: NILM with organisms (Candida, HSV, Enterobius)
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Organisms: [specify].
diagnoses.comment: Clinical correlation.
diagnoses.cat: Interpretation: NILM (Bethesda terminology, anal cytology)

categories.name: Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance
categories.definition: Changes suggestive of LSIL, insufficient for definitive diagnosis.

rom.source: SPANC cohort, histological HSIL PPV at baseline biopsy (Cancer Cytopathol, doi 10.1002/cncy.21936)
Systematic review & meta-analysis of anal cytology, risk of AIN2+ (PMC9588562)

categories.management: High-resolution anoscopy (HRA) with directed biopsy (IANS 2024 consensus / ANCHOR-era practice).
criteria: Criteria as cervical; nuclear enlargement 2.5–3× intermediate nucleus with mild hyperchromasia; atypical parakeratosis common.

diagnoses.name: ASC-US
diagnoses.final: Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US).
diagnoses.comment: HPV testing and/or high-resolution anoscopy recommended per local protocol.
diagnoses.cat: Interpretation: ASC-US (Bethesda terminology, anal cytology)

categories.name: Atypical squamous cells, cannot exclude HSIL
categories.definition: Changes suggestive of HSIL but insufficient.

rom.source: SPANC cohort, histological HSIL PPV at baseline biopsy (Cancer Cytopathol, doi 10.1002/cncy.21936)

categories.management: High-resolution anoscopy (HRA) with directed biopsy (IANS 2024 consensus / ANCHOR-era practice).
criteria: Small metaplastic-size cells with high N:C ratio; atypical keratinised small cells.

diagnoses.name: ASC-H
diagnoses.final: Atypical squamous cells, cannot exclude HSIL (ASC-H).
diagnoses.comment: High-resolution anoscopy with biopsy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Interpretation: ASC-H (Bethesda terminology, anal cytology)

categories.management: High-resolution anoscopy (HRA) with directed biopsy (IANS 2024 consensus / ANCHOR-era practice).
criteria: Koilocytes, binucleation, nuclear enlargement ≥3×, mature cytoplasm.

diagnoses.name: LSIL
diagnoses.final: Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL).
diagnoses.comment: High-resolution anoscopy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Interpretation: LSIL (Bethesda terminology, anal cytology)

categories.name: High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion
categories.definition: AIN2–3; precursor of anal SCC.

rom.source: SPANC cohort, histological HSIL PPV at baseline biopsy (Cancer Cytopathol, doi 10.1002/cncy.21936)
Systematic review & meta-analysis of anal cytology, risk of AIN2+ (PMC9588562)

criteria: Immature cells with high N:C ratio, hyperchromasia, irregular membranes; often keratinised in anal samples.

diagnoses.name: HSIL
diagnoses.final: High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL).
diagnoses.comment: High-resolution anoscopy with biopsy and treatment as per ANCHOR/IANS guidance.

systems.name: The Bethesda System (TBS) for Reporting Cervical Cytology
systems.specimen: Cervical/vaginal Pap smear – conventional and liquid-based (ThinPrep, SurePath)
use: All cervical and vaginal cytology specimens (screening and diagnostic), conventional or LBC.
Vaginal vault smears after hysterectomy.
Combined with HPV testing (co-testing/reflex) for risk-based management (ASCCP 2019).
not_use: Anal cytology – use the Bethesda terminology adapted for anal cytology (see Bethesda Anal).
Endometrial aspirates/brushings (no TBS categories – report descriptively).
Vulval scrapes and non-gynaecological specimens.
report_structure: Specimen adequacy (satisfactory/unsatisfactory, with transformation zone and quality indicators)
General categorization (optional): NILM / Other / Epithelial cell abnormality
Ancillary testing (e.g. HPV) and automated review if used
Educational notes and comments (optional, consistent with guidelines)

adequacy.title: Satisfactory for evaluation
items: Conventional smear: estimated ≥8,000–12,000 well-preserved, well-visualised squamous cells.
LBC (ThinPrep/SurePath): ≥5,000 well-visualised, well-preserved squamous cells.
Transformation zone (TZ) component: ≥10 well-preserved endocervical or squamous metaplastic cells (singly or in groups) – reported as present/absent, NOT a requirement for adequacy.
State quality indicators: partially obscured (50–75%), absence of TZ component, etc.

adequacy.title: Unsatisfactory for evaluation
items: Rejected/not processed: unlabelled specimen, broken slide, inadequate request.
Processed but unsatisfactory: inadequate squamous cellularity, or >75% of squamous cells obscured.
Any specimen with abnormal cells is satisfactory by definition.

adequacy.title: Special situations
items: Post-hysterectomy/vault and post-radiation/chemotherapy specimens may be judged on lower cellularity (≈2,000–5,000 cells) at the lab's discretion.
Bloody LBC samples: glacial acetic acid wash may salvage adequacy.

categories.name: Unsatisfactory for evaluation
categories.definition: Specimen cannot be reliably evaluated for epithelial abnormality. Either rejected/not processed (unlabelled, broken slide) or processed but unsatisfactory (cellularity or obscuring factors).

rom.source: TBS 2014

categories.management: Repeat cytology in 2–4 months (ASCCP 2019); if HPV co-test positive, colposcopy acceptable. Treat infection/atrophy before repeat if responsible.
criteria: Conventional smear: estimated <8,000–12,000 well-preserved, well-visualised squamous cells (use reference images; ≥5,000 not required to be counted).
Liquid-based: <5,000 well-visualised squamous cells (count fields at ×40/×10 per TBS table, at least 10 fields across diameter).
>75% of squamous cells obscured by blood, inflammation, thick areas, air-drying, contaminants (50–75% = satisfactory but partially obscured; mention as quality indicator).
Any specimen with abnormal cells (ASC-US or worse, AGC or worse) is by definition NOT unsatisfactory.
Rejected: unlabelled/mislabelled specimen, broken slide that cannot be repaired, inadequate requisition.

diagnoses.name: Unsatisfactory – scant squamous cellularity
diagnoses.final: Specimen adequacy: Unsatisfactory for evaluation – processed and examined, but unsatisfactory for evaluation of epithelial abnormality because of scant squamous cellularity.
diagnoses.comment: Suggest repeat cervical cytology in 2–4 months. If HPV test was performed and positive, colposcopy is advised as per ASCCP 2019.
diagnoses.cat: Specimen adequacy: Unsatisfactory for evaluation

diagnoses.name: Unsatisfactory – obscuring blood
diagnoses.final: Specimen adequacy: Unsatisfactory for evaluation – processed and examined, but more than 75% of squamous cells are obscured by blood.
diagnoses.comment: Suggest repeat sampling in 2–4 months, preferably avoiding menstruation; LBC may reduce obscuring blood.
diagnoses.cat: Specimen adequacy: Unsatisfactory for evaluation

diagnoses.name: Unsatisfactory – obscuring inflammation
diagnoses.final: Specimen adequacy: Unsatisfactory for evaluation – processed and examined, but more than 75% of squamous cells are obscured by inflammatory exudate.
diagnoses.comment: Suggest clinical evaluation/treatment of any infection and repeat cytology in 2–4 months.
diagnoses.cat: Specimen adequacy: Unsatisfactory for evaluation

diagnoses.name: Unsatisfactory – air-drying / poor fixation / thick smear
diagnoses.final: Specimen adequacy: Unsatisfactory for evaluation – processed and examined, but unsatisfactory due to air-drying artefact / poor fixation / thick smearing involving most of the cells.
diagnoses.comment: Suggest repeat sampling with immediate fixation in 95% ethanol (conventional) or LBC vial.
diagnoses.cat: Specimen adequacy: Unsatisfactory for evaluation

diagnoses.name: Rejected – unlabelled / broken slide
diagnoses.final: Specimen rejected/not processed because of [unlabelled specimen / broken slide / mismatch with requisition].
diagnoses.comment: Please resubmit a correctly labelled specimen with a completed requisition form.
diagnoses.cat: Specimen adequacy: Unsatisfactory for evaluation

categories.name: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
categories.definition: No cellular evidence of neoplasia. Organisms and other non-neoplastic findings are listed optionally.

rom.value: HPV-negative NILM: 5-year CIN3+ risk ≈0.1%; HPV-positive NILM: immediate CIN3+ risk ≈2–5% (ASCCP 2019 risk tables, approximate)
rom.source: ASCCP 2019 (approx.)

categories.management: Routine screening per age/HPV status. NILM + HPV-positive (non-16/18): repeat co-test in 1 year; HPV16/18 positive: colposcopy (ASCCP 2019).
criteria: Squamous cells: normal superficial/intermediate/parabasal with no nuclear atypia beyond reactive range.
May include organisms, reactive changes, atrophy, glandular cells post hysterectomy.
Transformation zone component (≥10 well-preserved endocervical or squamous metaplastic cells) is reported as a quality indicator, not an adequacy criterion.

diagnoses.name: Trichomonas vaginalis
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Organisms: Trichomonas vaginalis.
diagnoses.comment: Pear-shaped flagellate organisms with eccentric nuclei and eosinophilic cytoplasmic granules are seen. Suggest clinical correlation and treatment of patient and partner.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Organisms

diagnoses.name: Fungal organisms morphologically consistent with Candida spp.
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Organisms: Fungal organisms morphologically consistent with Candida spp.
diagnoses.comment: Pseudohyphae and yeast forms are seen, with 'shish-kebab' spearing of squamous cells. Suggest clinical correlation.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Organisms

diagnoses.name: Shift in flora suggestive of bacterial vaginosis
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Organisms: Shift in flora suggestive of bacterial vaginosis.
diagnoses.comment: Clue cells (squamous cells covered by coccobacilli obscuring the cell border) with a filmy coccobacillary background and paucity of lactobacilli. Clinical correlation (Amsel/Nugent criteria) recommended.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Organisms

diagnoses.name: Bacteria morphologically consistent with Actinomyces spp.
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Organisms: Bacteria morphologically consistent with Actinomyces spp.
diagnoses.comment: Tangled clumps of filamentous organisms with acute-angle branching ('cotton-ball' / woolly bodies) are seen; usually associated with an intrauterine device. Suggest clinical correlation.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Organisms

diagnoses.name: Cellular changes consistent with herpes simplex virus
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Organisms: Cellular changes consistent with herpes simplex virus.
diagnoses.comment: Multinucleated cells with nuclear moulding, margination of chromatin and ground-glass nuclei (3 Ms), with occasional Cowdry A intranuclear inclusions. Suggest clinical correlation.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Organisms

diagnoses.name: Cellular changes consistent with cytomegalovirus
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Organisms: Cellular changes consistent with cytomegalovirus.
diagnoses.comment: Enlarged (usually endocervical/glandular) cells with a single large intranuclear inclusion and halo, and small cytoplasmic inclusions. Rare; suggest clinical correlation, particularly immune status.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Organisms

diagnoses.name: Other organisms (Chlamydia-suggestive changes, Leptothrix, Enterobius ova, Schistosoma ova, etc.)
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Organisms: [specify, e.g. Leptothrix / Enterobius vermicularis ova / Schistosoma haematobium ova].
diagnoses.comment: TBS does not recommend a cytologic diagnosis of Chlamydia (nebular vacuoles are non-specific); advise NAAT if clinically suspected. Leptothrix often coexists with Trichomonas.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Organisms
diagnoses.note: Listed in TBS atlas as other findings; not a separate formal TBS term.

diagnoses.name: Reactive cellular changes associated with inflammation (includes typical repair)
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Other non-neoplastic findings: Reactive cellular changes associated with inflammation (includes typical repair).
diagnoses.comment: Mild nuclear enlargement with smooth membranes, fine chromatin and prominent nucleoli; repair shows flat cohesive sheets with streaming and no single atypical cells. Suggest treatment of cause and routine screening.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Reactive cellular changes

diagnoses.name: Reactive cellular changes associated with radiation
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Other non-neoplastic findings: Reactive cellular changes associated with radiation.
diagnoses.comment: Cellular and nuclear enlargement with preserved N:C ratio, bi/multinucleation, cytoplasmic vacuolation and polychromasia. History of radiotherapy noted; follow up as per oncology protocol.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Reactive cellular changes

diagnoses.name: Reactive cellular changes associated with intrauterine contraceptive device (IUD)
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Other non-neoplastic findings: Reactive cellular changes associated with intrauterine contraceptive device.
diagnoses.comment: Small clusters of glandular cells with vacuolated cytoplasm and occasional single cells with high N:C ratio; history of IUD helps avoid over-interpretation as AGC/HSIL.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Reactive cellular changes

diagnoses.name: Glandular cells status post hysterectomy
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Other non-neoplastic findings: Glandular cells status post hysterectomy.
diagnoses.comment: Benign-appearing glandular cells in a vaginal specimen after hysterectomy (e.g. adenosis, prolapsed tube, vaginal endometriosis). No further workup required.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Other non-neoplastic findings

diagnoses.name: Atrophy
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Other non-neoplastic findings: Atrophy.
diagnoses.comment: Predominantly parabasal cells in flat sheets with granular background, with or without inflammation ('atrophic vaginitis') or blue blobs. If atypia is equivocal, HPV testing or repeat after a short course of topical oestrogen may help.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Other non-neoplastic findings

diagnoses.name: Atrophic vaginitis (atrophy with inflammation)
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Other non-neoplastic findings: Atrophy with inflammation (atrophic vaginitis).
diagnoses.comment: Parabasal cells, granular necrotic-looking background, neutrophils and degenerate/pseudokeratotic cells; not to be mistaken for tumour diathesis. Suggest clinical correlation.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Other non-neoplastic findings

diagnoses.name: Keratotic changes (hyperkeratosis/parakeratosis) without atypia
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Squamous metaplasia / keratotic changes present.
diagnoses.comment: Anucleate squames and/or typical parakeratotic cells without nuclear atypia. May reflect prolapse or chronic irritation; correlate clinically.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Other non-neoplastic findings
diagnoses.note: Optional descriptor in TBS (non-neoplastic cellular variations).

diagnoses.name: Squamous metaplasia / tubal metaplasia
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM).
diagnoses.comment: Benign metaplastic squamous cells (and/or ciliated tubal-type cells). Reporting of these non-neoplastic variations is optional.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Non-neoplastic cellular variations

diagnoses.name: Pregnancy-associated changes (decidual cells, Arias-Stella reaction)
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM).
diagnoses.comment: Decidual cells / Arias-Stella-type glandular cells consistent with pregnancy-related change. Clinical history of pregnancy supports a benign interpretation.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Non-neoplastic cellular variations

diagnoses.name: Lymphocytic (follicular) cervicitis
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Other non-neoplastic findings: Reactive changes – follicular cervicitis.
diagnoses.comment: Polymorphous lymphoid cells including tingible-body macrophages; may mimic HSIL or lymphoma. Seen in chronic infection (incl. Chlamydia) and in postmenopausal women.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Reactive cellular changes

categories.line: General categorization: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy

categories.name: Other: Endometrial cells (in a woman ≥45 years)
categories.definition: Benign-appearing exfoliated endometrial cells in a woman aged 45 years or older; TBS 2014 raised the reporting age from 40 to 45. Not reported in women <45 years.

rom.value: Endometrial hyperplasia/carcinoma in ~0.5–2% (higher in postmenopausal women, especially with abnormal bleeding)
rom.source: Literature, approx.

categories.management: Endometrial evaluation only if postmenopausal (or abnormal bleeding/risk factors); not needed for asymptomatic premenopausal women (ASCCP).
criteria: Small tight 3-D balls of cells with scant cytoplasm, small dark nuclei, sometimes with a stromal core ('exodus' pattern).
No atypia (if atypical → AGC, endometrial).
Menstrual status/hormone therapy should be stated where known.

diagnoses.name: Endometrial cells present in a woman ≥45 years
diagnoses.final: Other: Endometrial cells present in a woman ≥45 years of age. Negative for squamous intraepithelial lesion.
diagnoses.comment: Benign-appearing endometrial cells are present. Endometrial evaluation is recommended if the patient is postmenopausal or has abnormal uterine bleeding; correlate with menstrual history and hormone therapy.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization: Other – see interpretation

diagnoses.name: Exfoliated endometrial stromal cells / histiocytes (≥45 y)
diagnoses.final: Other: Endometrial cells (stromal cells/histiocytes) present in a woman ≥45 years.
diagnoses.comment: TBS 2014 recommends not reporting isolated histiocytes; report only definite endometrial cells. Clinical correlation recommended.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization: Other – see interpretation

categories.name: Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance
categories.definition: Changes suggestive of LSIL that are qualitatively or quantitatively insufficient for a definitive interpretation.

rom.value: CIN2+ ≈5–10% on follow-up; CIN3+ immediate risk ≈4% if HPV-positive, <0.1% if HPV-negative (ASCCP 2019, approx.)
rom.source: Literature / ASCCP 2019

categories.management: Reflex HPV preferred. HPV-positive → colposcopy; HPV-negative → repeat co-test/HPV in 3 years (ASCCP 2019). Ages 21–24: repeat cytology at 1 year.
criteria: Nucleus 2.5–3× normal intermediate cell nucleus (≈35 µm²) or 2× squamous metaplastic nucleus.
Slightly increased N:C ratio, minimal hyperchromasia, mild irregularity of chromatin/nuclear outline.
Includes atypical parakeratosis and incomplete koilocytes.
Laboratory ASC:SIL ratio should be <3:1 (quality indicator); ASC rate typically ≤5%.

diagnoses.name: ASC-US
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US).
diagnoses.comment: Reflex high-risk HPV testing is recommended; management as per ASCCP 2019 risk-based guidelines.
diagnoses.cat: ASC-US – Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance

diagnoses.name: ASC-US in atrophic smear
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US). Background atrophy.
diagnoses.comment: Atypia may be related to atrophy; HPV testing or repeat cytology after a course of topical oestrogen may help clarify.
diagnoses.cat: ASC-US – Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance

diagnoses.name: ASC-US with atypical parakeratosis
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – ASC-US (atypical parakeratosis).
diagnoses.comment: Atypical parakeratotic cells with mildly enlarged dark nuclei. HPV testing recommended.
diagnoses.cat: ASC-US – Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance

categories.name: Atypical squamous cells, cannot exclude HSIL
categories.definition: Changes suggestive of HSIL but insufficient for a definitive interpretation; usually small (metaplastic-size) cells.

rom.value: CIN2+ ≈30–40%; immediate CIN3+ ≈26% if HPV-positive (ASCCP 2019, approx.)
rom.source: Literature / ASCCP 2019

categories.management: Colposcopy regardless of HPV result (ASCCP 2019).
criteria: Small sparse cells, metaplastic size, nucleus 1.5–2.5× normal, high N:C ratio approaching HSIL.
Crowded sheet pattern: tight 3-D groups with loss of polarity in which HSIL cannot be confirmed.
Atypical repair, severe atrophy or post-radiation atypia where HSIL cannot be excluded.

diagnoses.name: ASC-H
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – Atypical squamous cells, cannot exclude a high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (ASC-H).
diagnoses.comment: Colposcopy and directed biopsy are recommended as per ASCCP 2019, irrespective of HPV status.
diagnoses.cat: ASC-H – Atypical squamous cells, cannot exclude HSIL

categories.name: Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion
categories.definition: Encompasses HPV cytopathic effect / mild dysplasia / CIN 1.

rom.value: CIN2+ ≈15–30% on biopsy follow-up; immediate CIN3+ ≈4% if HPV-positive (ASCCP 2019, approx.)
rom.source: Literature / ASCCP 2019

categories.management: Colposcopy (HPV-positive or HPV not done); if HPV-negative, repeat co-test in 1 year acceptable (ASCCP 2019). Ages 21–24: repeat cytology at 1 year. Pregnancy: colposcopy may be deferred to postpartum.
criteria: Changes in mature (intermediate/superficial) squamous cells.
Nuclear enlargement ≥3× normal intermediate nucleus, hyperchromasia, irregular membranes, bi/multinucleation.
Koilocytes: sharply defined perinuclear cavitation with nuclear atypia (halo alone is not sufficient).
Keratinised cells with atypical nuclei can be LSIL.

diagnoses.name: LSIL (HPV cytopathic effect / mild dysplasia / CIN 1)
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL), encompassing HPV cytopathic effect / mild dysplasia / CIN 1.
diagnoses.comment: Colposcopic evaluation is recommended as per ASCCP 2019 risk-based management.
diagnoses.cat: LSIL – Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion

diagnoses.name: LSIL, cannot exclude HSIL (LSIL-H)
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL); a few cells suspicious for HSIL are present (cannot exclude HSIL).
diagnoses.comment: Colposcopy recommended. Some laboratories use this optional qualifier; it is not a formal TBS category.
diagnoses.note: Non-TBS optional qualifier used by some labs; TBS discourages new categories.
diagnoses.cat: LSIL – Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion

categories.name: High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion
categories.definition: Encompasses moderate and severe dysplasia, CIS, CIN 2 and CIN 3. Option to add 'with features suspicious for invasion'.

rom.value: CIN2+ ≈60–90%; immediate CIN3+ ≈49% if HPV-positive; invasive cancer ≈1–2% (ASCCP 2019 / literature, approx.)
rom.source: Literature / ASCCP 2019

categories.management: Expedited treatment (LEEP) or colposcopy with biopsy (ASCCP 2019); expedited treatment preferred for non-pregnant ≥25 years when immediate CIN3+ risk ≥60%.
criteria: Smaller, less mature cells (parabasal/metaplastic) than LSIL; high N:C ratio.
Hyperchromasia, coarse chromatin, irregular nuclear contours with notches/grooves; nucleoli usually absent.
Single cells, sheets or hyperchromatic crowded groups (syncytial).
Features suspicious for invasion: tumour diathesis, macronucleoli, bizarre keratinised cells.

diagnoses.name: HSIL (moderate dysplasia / CIN 2)
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL), encompassing moderate dysplasia / CIN 2.
diagnoses.comment: Colposcopy with biopsy or expedited treatment as per ASCCP 2019.
diagnoses.cat: HSIL – High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion

diagnoses.name: HSIL (severe dysplasia / CIS / CIN 3)
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL), encompassing severe dysplasia / carcinoma in situ / CIN 3.
diagnoses.comment: Colposcopy with biopsy or expedited excisional treatment as per ASCCP 2019.
diagnoses.cat: HSIL – High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion

diagnoses.name: HSIL with features suspicious for invasion
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) with features suspicious for invasion.
diagnoses.comment: Tumour diathesis / features raising concern for invasion are present. Urgent colposcopy and biopsy are recommended.
diagnoses.cat: HSIL – High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion

diagnoses.name: HSIL involving endocervical glands (crowded groups)
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL).
diagnoses.comment: HSIL cells are present in hyperchromatic crowded groups mimicking glandular lesions; flattening of cells at the periphery and absence of glandular features support HSIL with gland involvement.
diagnoses.cat: HSIL – High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion

categories.name: Squamous cell carcinoma
categories.definition: Malignant squamous neoplasm; TBS does not subclassify, but keratinising vs non-keratinising may be described.

rom.value: Invasive carcinoma confirmed in the large majority (PPV >80–90%)
rom.source: Literature, approx.

categories.management: Urgent colposcopy/biopsy and gynaecological oncology referral.
criteria: Keratinising: pleomorphic single cells (caudate, tadpole, spindle) with orangeophilic cytoplasm, dense hyperchromatic/pyknotic nuclei; less diathesis.
Non-keratinising: syncytial aggregates of cells with coarse irregular chromatin, prominent nucleoli and tumour diathesis (granular necrotic debris, old blood).
LBC: diathesis clings to cell clusters ('clinging diathesis').

diagnoses.name: Squamous cell carcinoma, keratinising type
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – Squamous cell carcinoma (keratinising type).
diagnoses.comment: Urgent colposcopy, biopsy and gynaecological oncology referral recommended.
diagnoses.cat: SCC – Squamous cell carcinoma

diagnoses.name: Squamous cell carcinoma, non-keratinising type
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – Squamous cell carcinoma (non-keratinising type).
diagnoses.comment: Urgent colposcopy, biopsy and gynaecological oncology referral recommended.
diagnoses.cat: SCC – Squamous cell carcinoma

diagnoses.name: Squamous cell carcinoma, NOS
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – Squamous cell carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Urgent colposcopy and biopsy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: SCC – Squamous cell carcinoma

categories.name: Atypical glandular cells
categories.definition: Glandular cells with nuclear atypia exceeding reactive/reparative change but lacking features of adenocarcinoma. Specify endocervical, endometrial or NOS; 'favor neoplastic' for endocervical or glandular NOS.

rom.value: Significant lesion (CIN2+/AIS/carcinoma) ≈9–38%; malignancy ≈3–17%; AGC-favor neoplastic markedly higher (≈27–96%)
rom.source: Literature, approx.

categories.management: AGC (all subtypes except atypical endometrial): colposcopy + endocervical sampling + endometrial sampling if ≥35 y or at risk. Atypical endometrial cells: endometrial and endocervical sampling first. AGC-favor neoplastic/AIS: diagnostic excision if no invasive disease (ASCCP 2019).
criteria: AGC endocervical NOS: sheets/strips with nuclear crowding, enlargement up to 3–5× normal endocervical nucleus, mild hyperchromasia, occasional nucleoli.
AGC endocervical, favor neoplastic: feathering/rosettes/strips but quantitatively or qualitatively short of AIS.
AGC endometrial: small groups, nuclei slightly enlarged, mild hyperchromasia, small nucleoli, ill-defined vacuolated cytoplasm.
AGC NOS: cell origin cannot be determined.

diagnoses.name: Atypical endocervical cells, NOS
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Glandular cell – Atypical endocervical cells, not otherwise specified (AGC, endocervical NOS).
diagnoses.comment: Colposcopy with endocervical sampling (and endometrial sampling if ≥35 years or at risk) is recommended (ASCCP 2019).
diagnoses.cat: AGC – Atypical glandular cells

diagnoses.name: Atypical endometrial cells, NOS
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Glandular cell – Atypical endometrial cells.
diagnoses.comment: Endometrial and endocervical sampling is recommended; colposcopy if no endometrial pathology is found (ASCCP 2019).
diagnoses.cat: AGC – Atypical glandular cells

diagnoses.name: Atypical glandular cells, NOS
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Glandular cell – Atypical glandular cells, not otherwise specified (AGC NOS).
diagnoses.comment: Colposcopy with endocervical sampling, plus endometrial sampling if ≥35 years or at risk, is recommended.
diagnoses.cat: AGC – Atypical glandular cells

diagnoses.name: Atypical endocervical cells, favor neoplastic
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Glandular cell – Atypical endocervical cells, favor neoplastic.
diagnoses.comment: Colposcopy with endocervical sampling; if no invasive disease, a diagnostic excisional procedure is recommended (ASCCP 2019).
diagnoses.cat: AGC – Atypical glandular cells

diagnoses.name: Atypical glandular cells, favor neoplastic
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Glandular cell – Atypical glandular cells, favor neoplastic.
diagnoses.comment: Colposcopy, endocervical and endometrial sampling; diagnostic excision if no invasive disease is identified.
diagnoses.cat: AGC – Atypical glandular cells

categories.name: Endocervical adenocarcinoma in situ
categories.definition: Non-invasive high-grade endocervical glandular lesion (HPV-associated).

rom.value: AIS or invasive adenocarcinoma on follow-up in the majority (≈50–90%); concurrent invasive adenocarcinoma in a subset
rom.source: Literature, approx.

categories.management: Colposcopy, endocervical sampling and diagnostic excision (cold-knife cone preferred, intact specimen); hysterectomy after excision for most (ASCCP 2019).
criteria: Crowded sheets/strips with nuclear pseudostratification, feathering at edges, rosettes.
Enlarged elongated hyperchromatic nuclei, coarse even chromatin, mitoses and apoptotic bodies; nucleoli small or inconspicuous.
Clean background (no tumour diathesis).

diagnoses.name: Endocervical adenocarcinoma in situ (AIS)
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Glandular cell – Endocervical adenocarcinoma in situ (AIS).
diagnoses.comment: Colposcopy, endocervical sampling and diagnostic excisional procedure are recommended as per ASCCP 2019.
diagnoses.cat: AIS – Endocervical adenocarcinoma in situ

categories.name: Adenocarcinoma
categories.definition: Malignant glandular neoplasm; specify endocervical, endometrial, extrauterine or NOS when possible.

rom.source: Literature, approx.

categories.management: Urgent gynaecological oncology referral; colposcopy/biopsy, endometrial sampling and imaging as appropriate.
criteria: Endocervical: abundant columnar cells in sheets/3-D clusters/single cells, enlarged pleomorphic nuclei, macronucleoli, tumour diathesis.
Endometrial: small 3-D clusters/single cells, nuclear size increasing with grade, prominent nucleoli, vacuolated cytoplasm, 'watery' finely granular diathesis, neutrophils within cytoplasm.
Extrauterine: clean background (no diathesis), papillary clusters/psammoma bodies (ovarian serous) or signet-ring cells (GI).

diagnoses.name: Adenocarcinoma, endocervical
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Glandular cell – Adenocarcinoma, endocervical.
diagnoses.comment: Urgent colposcopy/biopsy and gynaecological oncology referral recommended.
diagnoses.cat: ADCA – Adenocarcinoma

diagnoses.name: Adenocarcinoma, endometrial
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Glandular cell – Adenocarcinoma, endometrial.
diagnoses.comment: Endometrial sampling and gynaecological oncology referral recommended.
diagnoses.cat: ADCA – Adenocarcinoma

diagnoses.name: Adenocarcinoma, extrauterine
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Glandular cell – Adenocarcinoma, extrauterine.
diagnoses.comment: Clean background suggests an extrauterine source (e.g. ovary, fallopian tube, GI tract, breast). Clinical and radiological evaluation for a primary is recommended.
diagnoses.cat: ADCA – Adenocarcinoma

diagnoses.name: Adenocarcinoma, NOS
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Glandular cell – Adenocarcinoma, not otherwise specified.
diagnoses.comment: Site of origin cannot be determined cytologically. Further clinical, colposcopic and endometrial evaluation is recommended.
diagnoses.cat: ADCA – Adenocarcinoma

categories.name: Other malignant neoplasms
categories.definition: Malignant neoplasms that are neither squamous nor glandular (specify).

rom.source: Literature

categories.management: Biopsy and ancillary studies; oncology referral.
criteria: Small cell / high-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma: small cells with moulding, salt-and-pepper chromatin, crush artefact.
Carcinosarcoma (malignant mixed Müllerian tumour), sarcomas, melanoma, lymphoma, metastatic tumours.
Cell block/IHC on residual LBC can help.

diagnoses.name: Small cell (high-grade neuroendocrine) carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Other malignant neoplasm: Malignant cells consistent with small cell (high-grade neuroendocrine) carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Biopsy with neuroendocrine IHC (synaptophysin, chromogranin, INSM1) recommended.
diagnoses.cat: OMN – Other malignant neoplasms

diagnoses.name: Carcinosarcoma (malignant mixed Müllerian tumour)
diagnoses.final: Other malignant neoplasm: Malignant cells with epithelial and spindle/sarcomatous components, suggestive of carcinosarcoma.
diagnoses.comment: Endometrial sampling and histological confirmation recommended.
diagnoses.cat: OMN – Other malignant neoplasms

diagnoses.name: Sarcoma (e.g. leiomyosarcoma, embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma)
diagnoses.final: Other malignant neoplasm: Malignant spindle/round cells, suggestive of sarcoma.
diagnoses.comment: Biopsy with IHC recommended for classification.
diagnoses.cat: OMN – Other malignant neoplasms

diagnoses.name: Malignant melanoma
diagnoses.final: Other malignant neoplasm: Malignant cells suggestive of melanoma.
diagnoses.comment: Melanin pigment / prominent nucleoli; confirm with S100/SOX10/HMB45/Melan-A on biopsy or cell block; exclude metastasis.
diagnoses.cat: OMN – Other malignant neoplasms

diagnoses.name: Lymphoma
diagnoses.final: Other malignant neoplasm: Atypical lymphoid population suspicious for lymphoma.
diagnoses.comment: Biopsy with IHC/flow cytometry recommended; distinguish from follicular cervicitis.
diagnoses.cat: OMN – Other malignant neoplasms

diagnoses.name: Metastatic carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Other malignant neoplasm: Malignant cells consistent with metastatic carcinoma (specify likely primary if possible).
diagnoses.comment: Clinical history and IHC on biopsy/cell block are recommended to establish the primary site.
diagnoses.cat: OMN – Other malignant neoplasms

extra.title: HPV and management pointers (ASCCP 2019, risk-based)
items: Management is based on the patient's immediate and 5-year CIN3+ risk combining current result and history, not on cytology alone.
Primary HPV screening (FDA-approved assays) every 5 years from age 25 (ACS 2020) or co-testing every 5 years 30–65 / cytology every 3 years 21–29 (USPSTF).
HPV16/18 positive with NILM → colposcopy; other HR-HPV positive with NILM → 1-year repeat.
Use the ASCCP risk tables/app for individual decisions; WHO 2021 guidance favours HPV-DNA primary screening in low-resource settings.

references: Nayar R, Wilbur DC (eds). The Bethesda System for Reporting Cervical Cytology: Definitions, Criteria, and Explanatory Notes. 3rd ed. Springer, 2015.
Perkins RB, et al. 2019 ASCCP Risk-Based Management Consensus Guidelines for Abnormal Cervical Cancer Screening Tests and Cancer Precursors. J Low Genit Tract Dis. 2020;24(2):102–131.
WHO guideline for screening and treatment of cervical pre-cancer lesions for cervical cancer prevention, 2nd ed. WHO, 2021.

systems.name: The Bethesda System for Reporting Thyroid Cytopathology (TBSRTC)
systems.specimen: Thyroid FNA (US-guided or palpation), smears, LBC, cell block
use: All thyroid FNA specimens in adults and children.
Lymph node FNA for suspected metastatic thyroid carcinoma can use the same terminology (with Tg washout).
Every report should begin with one of the six category names (numbers optional but recommended alongside the name).
not_use: Non-thyroidal neck masses (use Milan for salivary, Sydney for lymph node).
Parathyroid lesions intentionally sampled (report descriptively + PTH washout).
Frozen sections/histology.
report_structure: Specimen and site/nodule (side, size, TI-RADS if provided)
Diagnostic category name (± number), e.g. 'Benign (Bethesda II)'

adequacy.title: Adequate
items: At least 6 groups of well-visualised follicular cells, each with ≥10 cells, preferably on a single slide.

Exceptions (adequate regardless of count): solid nodules with cytologic atypia (any significant atypia → report it); solid nodules with inflammation (e.g. lymphocytic thyroiditis, abscess, granulomatous thyroiditis); colloid nodules with abundant thick colloid (benign).
Cell block/LBC can contribute to cellularity.

adequacy.title: Nondiagnostic
items: Below threshold; cyst fluid only (macrophages); blood only; obscuring artefact; poor fixation/staining.
Two consecutive ND results: correlate with US; consider core biopsy or surgery if suspicious.

categories.name: Nondiagnostic
categories.definition: Specimen does not meet adequacy criteria (except exceptions listed) or is uninterpretable because of preparation artefact.

rom.source: TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)
TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)

categories.management: Repeat FNA with ultrasound guidance (no minimum wait required). Persistently ND solid nodules: close follow-up or surgery.
criteria: Fewer than 6 groups of ≥10 well-preserved, well-stained follicular cells.
Poorly prepared, poorly stained or obscured follicular cells (blood, thick smears, air-drying).
Cyst fluid only (macrophages ± few cells) – report as ND, 'cyst fluid only' and correlate with US (purely cystic, no worrisome features may be followed).

diagnoses.name: Nondiagnostic – insufficient follicular cells
diagnoses.final: Nondiagnostic (TBSRTC Category I). Insufficient follicular epithelial cells for evaluation.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat ultrasound-guided FNA is recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category I – Nondiagnostic

diagnoses.name: Nondiagnostic – cyst fluid only
diagnoses.final: Nondiagnostic (TBSRTC Category I) – cyst fluid only.
diagnoses.comment: Only macrophages/cyst contents are present without adequate follicular cells. Correlate with ultrasound; repeat FNA of any solid component is recommended if clinically/radiologically indicated.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category I – Nondiagnostic

diagnoses.name: Nondiagnostic – blood only / obscured
diagnoses.final: Nondiagnostic (TBSRTC Category I). Specimen consists predominantly of blood; follicular cells are scant/obscured.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat ultrasound-guided FNA is recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category I – Nondiagnostic

diagnoses.name: Nondiagnostic – poor preservation/air-drying artefact
diagnoses.final: Nondiagnostic (TBSRTC Category I) due to air-drying/preparation artefact.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat FNA with optimal smear preparation/fixation is recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category I – Nondiagnostic

categories.name: Benign
categories.definition: Benign follicular nodule, thyroiditis or other benign finding.

rom.source: TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)
TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)

categories.management: Clinical and sonographic follow-up; repeat FNA only if growth or suspicious US features.
criteria: Benign follicular nodule: adequate follicular cells in flat sheets/macrofollicles, honeycomb, abundant colloid; macrophages; no significant atypia.
Abundant thin/thick colloid with few cells is acceptable as benign.
Thyroiditis: lymphoid cells ± oncocytes (Hashimoto), granulomas (subacute), neutrophils (acute).

diagnoses.name: Benign follicular nodule (adenomatoid/colloid nodule, nodular goitre)
diagnoses.final: Benign (TBSRTC Category II). Consistent with a benign follicular nodule.
diagnoses.comment: Smears show abundant colloid and benign follicular cells in flat sheets with macrophages. Clinical and ultrasound follow-up recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category II – Benign

diagnoses.name: Graves disease (diffuse hyperplasia)
diagnoses.final: Benign (TBSRTC Category II). Benign follicular cells, consistent with Graves disease in the appropriate clinical context.
diagnoses.comment: Flame cells/marginal vacuoles may be present; correlate with thyroid function tests and antibodies.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category II – Benign

diagnoses.name: Chronic lymphocytic (Hashimoto) thyroiditis
diagnoses.final: Benign (TBSRTC Category II). Consistent with chronic lymphocytic (Hashimoto) thyroiditis in the proper clinical context.
diagnoses.comment: Polymorphous lymphoid cells with oncocytic follicular cells. Correlate with anti-TPO/anti-Tg antibodies. If a dominant monotonous lymphoid population is present, flow cytometry is advised to exclude lymphoma.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category II – Benign

diagnoses.name: Subacute granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis
diagnoses.final: Benign (TBSRTC Category II). Consistent with granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
diagnoses.comment: Epithelioid granulomas and multinucleated giant cells engulfing colloid with degenerated follicular cells; clinical correlation (painful gland, raised ESR) recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category II – Benign

diagnoses.name: Acute (suppurative) thyroiditis
diagnoses.final: Benign (TBSRTC Category II). Acute suppurative thyroiditis.
diagnoses.comment: Neutrophils, necrotic debris and macrophages. Culture is recommended; consider pyriform sinus fistula in children.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category II – Benign

diagnoses.name: Riedel thyroiditis / IgG4-related thyroiditis
diagnoses.final: Benign (TBSRTC Category II) – scant fibrous stromal fragments with few inflammatory cells; findings may be compatible with Riedel (IgG4-related) thyroiditis in the right context.
diagnoses.comment: Aspirates are often scant/nondiagnostic; biopsy and IgG4 correlation needed.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category II – Benign

diagnoses.name: Benign cyst / cystic degeneration with follicular cells
diagnoses.final: Benign (TBSRTC Category II). Benign follicular nodule with cystic change.
diagnoses.comment: Macrophages, colloid and adequate benign follicular cells. Follow-up recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category II – Benign

diagnoses.name: Black thyroid / amyloid / other benign
diagnoses.final: Benign (TBSRTC Category II). [Specify benign finding].
diagnoses.comment: Correlate clinically.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category II – Benign

categories.name: Atypia of undetermined significance (AUS)
categories.definition: Cells with architectural and/or nuclear atypia not sufficient for FN, SFM or malignant. 3rd ed: single term AUS (FLUS removed); subcategorize as AUS-nuclear or AUS-other.

rom.source: TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)
TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)

categories.management: Repeat FNA, molecular testing, diagnostic lobectomy or surveillance. Paediatric: repeat FNA or surgery (molecular testing not established). Lab AUS rate should be ≤10%.
criteria: AUS-nuclear: focal nuclear atypia (enlargement, pallor, grooves, irregular contours) in otherwise benign aspirate; extensive but mild atypia; atypical cyst-lining cells; 'histiocytoid' cells.
AUS-other (architectural): prominent microfollicles/crowding in a sparse aspirate insufficient for FN.

AUS-other: predominance of oncocytic cells in sparse aspirate with scant colloid; atypical lymphoid cells (flow recommended); atypia not otherwise categorised (e.g. psammoma bodies without PTC nuclei).
Recommended: specify subtype in report; nuclear atypia carries higher ROM.

diagnoses.name: AUS – nuclear atypia
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance (TBSRTC Category III) – AUS-nuclear (cytologic atypia).
diagnoses.comment: Focal nuclear changes (enlargement, pallor, grooves) are present but insufficient for suspicious for PTC. Repeat FNA and/or molecular testing is suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category III – AUS

diagnoses.name: AUS – architectural atypia (microfollicles)
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance (TBSRTC Category III) – AUS-other (architectural atypia).
diagnoses.comment: Scant aspirate with predominant microfollicles insufficient for follicular neoplasm. Repeat FNA and/or molecular testing is suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category III – AUS

diagnoses.name: AUS – nuclear and architectural atypia
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance (TBSRTC Category III) – AUS-nuclear and architectural.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat FNA, molecular testing or diagnostic lobectomy as clinically appropriate.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category III – AUS

diagnoses.name: AUS – oncocytic cell predominance (sparse)
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance (TBSRTC Category III) – AUS-other (oncocytic cells).
diagnoses.comment: Sparse aspirate composed predominantly of oncocytic cells with scant colloid; clinical context (e.g. Hashimoto, multinodular goitre) may favour benign. Repeat FNA/molecular testing suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category III – AUS

diagnoses.name: AUS – atypical lymphoid cells
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance (TBSRTC Category III) – AUS-other (atypical lymphoid cells, lymphoma not excluded).
diagnoses.comment: Repeat FNA with material for flow cytometry is recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category III – AUS

diagnoses.name: AUS – atypical cyst-lining cells
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance (TBSRTC Category III) – AUS-nuclear (atypical cyst lining cells).
diagnoses.comment: Likely reactive cyst-lining cells but PTC cannot be excluded; repeat FNA of solid area suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category III – AUS

diagnoses.name: AUS – psammoma bodies without diagnostic nuclear features
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance (TBSRTC Category III) – AUS-other.
diagnoses.comment: Psammoma bodies without papillary carcinoma nuclear features. Repeat FNA suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category III – AUS

categories.name: Follicular neoplasm (FN)
categories.definition: Moderately to highly cellular aspirate of follicular cells with marked crowding/microfollicles, or composed exclusively of oncocytic cells (FN, oncocytic type). Includes cases with mild nuclear changes (to account for NIFTP/follicular-pattern tumours).

rom.source: TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)
TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)

categories.management: Molecular testing and/or diagnostic lobectomy. Paediatric: surgery.
criteria: Cellular aspirate with predominant microfollicles/trabeculae, crowding and overlapping; scant colloid.
Mild nuclear changes (enlargement, chromatin pallor) allowed if no true PTC nuclei (papillae, pseudoinclusions absent).
FN oncocytic type: almost exclusively oncocytic cells (abundant granular cytoplasm, prominent nucleoli), few/no lymphocytes or colloid.

diagnoses.name: Follicular neoplasm
diagnoses.final: Follicular neoplasm (TBSRTC Category IV).
diagnoses.comment: Cellular aspirate of follicular cells in microfollicles with scant colloid. Differential includes follicular adenoma, follicular carcinoma, follicular-pattern PTC/NIFTP and adenomatous nodule. Molecular testing and/or lobectomy suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category IV – Follicular neoplasm

diagnoses.name: Follicular neoplasm, oncocytic (Hürthle cell) type
diagnoses.final: Follicular neoplasm, oncocytic (formerly Hürthle cell) type (TBSRTC Category IV).
diagnoses.comment: Aspirate composed almost exclusively of oncocytic cells. Differential includes oncocytic adenoma/carcinoma and oncocytic hyperplastic nodule. Molecular testing and/or lobectomy suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category IV – Follicular neoplasm

diagnoses.name: Follicular neoplasm with mild nuclear changes (NIFTP/follicular variant PTC in differential)
diagnoses.final: Follicular neoplasm (TBSRTC Category IV). Mild nuclear changes are present.
diagnoses.comment: Differential includes NIFTP, invasive encapsulated follicular variant PTC and follicular adenoma/carcinoma. Lobectomy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category IV – Follicular neoplasm

diagnoses.name: Hyalinizing trabecular tumour (favored)
diagnoses.final: Follicular neoplasm (TBSRTC Category IV), favouring hyalinizing trabecular tumour (or Suspicious for malignancy depending on nuclear features).
diagnoses.comment: Cohesive cells around hyaline material, grooves and pseudoinclusions; Ki-67 (MIB-1) membranous staining supports. Lobectomy suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category IV – Follicular neoplasm
diagnoses.note: HTT may be categorised as FN or SFM depending on features.

diagnoses.name: Parathyroid tissue (intrathyroidal) suspected
diagnoses.final: Follicular neoplasm (TBSRTC Category IV) – cannot exclude parathyroid tissue.
diagnoses.comment: Immunostains (GATA3, PTH, chromogranin; TTF1/Tg negative) or PTH washout measurement suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category IV – Follicular neoplasm

categories.name: Suspicious for malignancy (SFM)
categories.definition: Features strongly suspicious but insufficient for definitive malignancy. Specify: suspicious for PTC, MTC, lymphoma, metastatic, other.

rom.source: TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)
TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)

categories.management: Molecular testing, lobectomy or near-total thyroidectomy.
criteria: Suspicious for PTC: patchy nuclear changes, incomplete nuclear changes, sparse cells with PTC features, or cystic degeneration pattern.
Suspicious for MTC: monomorphic plasmacytoid/spindle cells with salt-and-pepper chromatin, insufficient material for IHC (calcitonin, CEA).
Suspicious for lymphoma: monomorphic lymphoid cells; flow cytometry needed.
Suspicious for malignancy, other (e.g. metastasis, ATC).

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for papillary thyroid carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy (TBSRTC Category V) – suspicious for papillary thyroid carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Some nuclear features of PTC are present but are focal/incomplete. Molecular testing or surgery recommended; NIFTP is in the differential.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category V – Suspicious for malignancy

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for medullary thyroid carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy (TBSRTC Category V) – suspicious for medullary thyroid carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Serum calcitonin and CEA, and calcitonin immunostain on repeat FNA/cell block, are recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category V – Suspicious for malignancy

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for lymphoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy (TBSRTC Category V) – suspicious for lymphoma.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat FNA for flow cytometry or core biopsy is recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category V – Suspicious for malignancy

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for metastatic malignancy
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy (TBSRTC Category V) – suspicious for metastatic [carcinoma/melanoma].
diagnoses.comment: Clinical history and IHC on cell block suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category V – Suspicious for malignancy

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for malignancy, other (e.g. anaplastic carcinoma)
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy (TBSRTC Category V) – suspicious for [specify].
diagnoses.comment: Further sampling/biopsy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category V – Suspicious for malignancy

categories.name: Malignant
categories.definition: Cytomorphologic features conclusive for malignancy; specify type.

rom.source: TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)
TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)

categories.management: Lobectomy or near-total thyroidectomy (PTC/follicular-derived); MTC, ATC, lymphoma and metastases managed by tumour-specific protocols. Active surveillance may be an option for papillary microcarcinoma.
criteria: PTC: papillae/sheets, enlarged oval overlapping nuclei, pale powdery chromatin, grooves, intranuclear pseudoinclusions, psammoma bodies, ropy colloid, multinucleate giant cells.
MTC: dispersed plasmacytoid/spindle/round cells, salt-and-pepper chromatin, red cytoplasmic granules (MGG), amyloid; calcitonin+.
High-grade follicular-derived (poorly differentiated/DHGTC): insular/solid/trabecular, scant colloid, mitoses, necrosis.
ATC: markedly pleomorphic epithelioid/spindle/giant cells, necrosis, neutrophils.
Lymphoma, SCC, metastases.

diagnoses.name: Papillary thyroid carcinoma (classic)
diagnoses.final: Malignant (TBSRTC Category VI) – papillary thyroid carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Diagnostic nuclear features of PTC (enlarged overlapping oval nuclei, powdery chromatin, grooves and intranuclear pseudoinclusions) with papillary fragments and psammoma bodies.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Papillary thyroid carcinoma, follicular subtype
diagnoses.final: Malignant (TBSRTC Category VI) – papillary thyroid carcinoma, consistent with follicular subtype.
diagnoses.comment: Microfollicles with well-developed PTC nuclear features. NIFTP cannot be excluded cytologically for encapsulated lesions; histology required.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Papillary thyroid carcinoma, tall cell subtype
diagnoses.final: Malignant (TBSRTC Category VI) – papillary thyroid carcinoma, with features suggestive of tall cell subtype.
diagnoses.comment: Cells 2–3× taller than wide with abundant oncocytic cytoplasm and frequent pseudoinclusions; aggressive subtype – histological confirmation required.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Papillary thyroid carcinoma, other subtypes (columnar, hobnail, diffuse sclerosing, Warthin-like, oncocytic, solid, cribriform-morular*)
diagnoses.final: Malignant (TBSRTC Category VI) – papillary thyroid carcinoma, [subtype] features.
diagnoses.comment: *Cribriform-morular thyroid carcinoma is a separate entity in WHO 2022 (CTNNB1/APC; β-catenin nuclear positivity; consider FAP).
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Medullary thyroid carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (TBSRTC Category VI) – medullary thyroid carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Confirmed by calcitonin positivity / elevated serum calcitonin. Recommend serum calcitonin, CEA, RET germline testing and pheochromocytoma screening.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Poorly differentiated / high-grade follicular-derived carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (TBSRTC Category VI) – carcinoma, consistent with poorly differentiated (high-grade follicular cell-derived) thyroid carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Solid/insular/trabecular groups, scant colloid, mitoses and necrosis; TTF1/PAX8/thyroglobulin positive.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Anaplastic (undifferentiated) thyroid carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (TBSRTC Category VI) – anaplastic thyroid carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Highly pleomorphic malignant cells with necrosis. Urgent oncology referral; BRAF V600E testing recommended for targeted therapy.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Squamous cell carcinoma of thyroid
diagnoses.final: Malignant (TBSRTC Category VI) – squamous cell carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: WHO 2022 classifies primary thyroid SCC as a pattern of anaplastic carcinoma; exclude direct extension or metastasis (larynx, oesophagus).
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Lymphoma (e.g. DLBCL, MALT lymphoma)
diagnoses.final: Malignant (TBSRTC Category VI) – non-Hodgkin lymphoma [type if determined].
diagnoses.comment: Flow cytometry/IHC confirm; low-grade MALT lymphoma often needs histology.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Metastatic malignancy
diagnoses.final: Malignant (TBSRTC Category VI) – metastatic [carcinoma/melanoma], consistent with [primary].
diagnoses.comment: Common primaries: kidney, lung, breast, melanoma. IHC on cell block recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Follicular / oncocytic carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Not diagnosable on cytology – report as Follicular neoplasm (Category IV).
diagnoses.comment: Capsular/vascular invasion cannot be assessed on FNA.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category IV – Follicular neoplasm (not VI)
diagnoses.note: Included for search: follicular carcinoma is never Category VI on FNA.

extra.title: Paediatric notes (3rd ed)
items: ROMs are higher in children for every category (ND 14%, B 6%, AUS 28%, FN 50%, SFM 81%, MAL 98%).
Molecular testing is not yet standard; AUS → repeat FNA or surgery, FN → surgery (lobectomy/thyroidectomy).

extra.title: NIFTP impact
items: 3rd ed quotes ROM with NIFTP counted as malignant; where NIFTP is excluded, ROM falls (largest drop in FN, SFM, AUS).
Avoid diagnosing 'malignant – PTC' for purely follicular-patterned lesions with subtle nuclear changes; use SFM or FN.

extra.title: Molecular testing
items: Afirma GSC/XA, ThyroSeq v3, ThyGeNEXT/ThyraMIR are used for AUS/FN to refine risk (where available).

references: Ali SZ, VanderLaan PA (eds). The Bethesda System for Reporting Thyroid Cytopathology: Definitions, Criteria, and Explanatory Notes. 3rd ed. Springer, 2023.
Ali SZ, Baloch ZW, Cochand-Priollet B, et al. The 2023 Bethesda System for Reporting Thyroid Cytopathology. Thyroid. 2023;33(9):1039–1044.
WHO Classification of Tumours Editorial Board. Endocrine and Neuroendocrine Tumours. 5th ed. IARC, 2022.

systems.name: The Milan System for Reporting Salivary Gland Cytopathology (MSRSGC)
systems.specimen: Major and minor salivary gland FNA
use: FNA of major (parotid, submandibular, sublingual) and minor salivary glands and periparotid/submandibular masses.
not_use: Cervical lymph nodes outside the gland (use Sydney/WHO LN).
Thyroid or other neck masses.
report_structure: Ancillary tests (IHC/FISH e.g. PLAG1, MYB, MAML2, NR4A3, pan-TRK)

adequacy.title: Adequacy
items: Specimen adequate if it contains enough lesional material to answer the clinical question.
Guide: a minimum of ~60 lesional cells in solid lesions (2nd ed); matrix alone (e.g. chondromyxoid) may be diagnostic.
Mucinous cyst fluid is not ND (→ AUS); any atypia is not ND.
ROSE and US guidance reduce ND rates.

categories.name: Non-diagnostic
categories.definition: Insufficient cellular material for a cytological diagnosis.

rom.source: Milan 2nd ed (Rossi et al., Cancer Cytopathol 2024, doi 10.1002/cncy.22753, Table 1)

categories.management: Clinical and radiological correlation; repeat FNA (ideally ultrasound-guided ± ROSE). [Milan 2nd ed; Rossi et al. Cancer Cytopathol 2024 and review in IP Arch Cytol Histopathol Res]
criteria: Fewer than 60 lesional cells (2nd ed guidance) in a solid lesion, with no matrix/specific findings.
Poor preservation, obscuring blood/artefact.
Non-mucinous cyst fluid with only macrophages/no epithelium.
Exception: any atypia → not ND; mucinous cyst fluid → AUS (not ND).

diagnoses.name: Non-diagnostic – insufficient cellularity
diagnoses.final: Non-diagnostic (Milan Category I). Insufficient lesional cells for diagnosis.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat ultrasound-guided FNA or core biopsy if clinically indicated.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System I – Non-diagnostic

diagnoses.name: Non-diagnostic – non-mucinous cyst contents only
diagnoses.final: Non-diagnostic (Milan Category I). Non-mucinous cyst contents with macrophages only.
diagnoses.comment: Correlate with imaging; repeat FNA of any solid component.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System I – Non-diagnostic

diagnoses.name: Non-diagnostic – normal salivary elements only (lesion not sampled)
diagnoses.final: Non-diagnostic (Milan Category I). Normal salivary gland elements only in the setting of a discrete mass.
diagnoses.comment: May not represent the lesion; repeat image-guided FNA recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System I – Non-diagnostic

categories.name: Non-neoplastic
categories.definition: Benign non-neoplastic processes: inflammatory, reactive, cystic, infectious.

rom.source: Milan 2nd ed (Rossi et al., Cancer Cytopathol 2024, doi 10.1002/cncy.22753, Table 1)

categories.management: Clinical follow-up with clinical and imaging correlation (to catch an under-sampled neoplasm). [Milan 2nd ed; Rossi et al. Cancer Cytopathol 2024 and review in IP Arch Cytol Histopathol Res]
criteria: Sialadenitis (acute/chronic/granulomatous), sialadenosis, reactive lymph node, benign cysts (lymphoepithelial cyst).
Normal salivary elements with no discrete mass clinically.

diagnoses.name: Chronic sialadenitis
diagnoses.final: Non-neoplastic (Milan Category II). Chronic sialadenitis.
diagnoses.comment: Scant acinar cells, ductal groups, lymphocytes and fibrous fragments. Clinical follow-up.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System II – Non-neoplastic

diagnoses.name: Acute sialadenitis / abscess
diagnoses.final: Non-neoplastic (Milan Category II). Acute sialadenitis.
diagnoses.comment: Neutrophils and debris; culture recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System II – Non-neoplastic

diagnoses.name: Granulomatous sialadenitis (TB, sarcoidosis, duct obstruction)
diagnoses.final: Non-neoplastic (Milan Category II). Granulomatous sialadenitis.
diagnoses.comment: ZN stain/CBNAAT recommended to exclude tuberculosis.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System II – Non-neoplastic

diagnoses.name: Sialadenosis
diagnoses.final: Non-neoplastic (Milan Category II). Consistent with sialadenosis in the appropriate clinical setting.
diagnoses.comment: Enlarged acinar cells; associated with diabetes, alcohol, malnutrition, bulimia.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System II – Non-neoplastic

diagnoses.name: Reactive intraparotid lymph node
diagnoses.final: Non-neoplastic (Milan Category II). Reactive lymphoid hyperplasia (intraparotid lymph node).
diagnoses.comment: Polymorphous lymphoid cells; if monotonous, flow cytometry to exclude lymphoma.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System II – Non-neoplastic

diagnoses.name: Lymphoepithelial cyst (incl. HIV-associated)
diagnoses.final: Non-neoplastic (Milan Category II). Consistent with lymphoepithelial cyst.
diagnoses.comment: Squames, lymphocytes and cyst debris; HIV testing if multiple/bilateral. Exclude Warthin tumour and cystic SCC metastasis.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System II – Non-neoplastic

diagnoses.name: IgG4-related / chronic sclerosing sialadenitis (Küttner)
diagnoses.final: Non-neoplastic (Milan Category II). Chronic sclerosing sialadenitis.
diagnoses.comment: Serum IgG4 and histology for confirmation.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System II – Non-neoplastic

diagnoses.name: Sjögren / lymphoepithelial sialadenitis
diagnoses.final: Non-neoplastic (Milan Category II). Lymphoepithelial sialadenitis.
diagnoses.comment: Risk of MALT lymphoma; flow cytometry if a monotonous population is present.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System II – Non-neoplastic

categories.name: Atypia of undetermined significance (AUS)
categories.definition: Indeterminate lesion where neoplasm cannot be excluded; mostly reactive/metaplastic atypia or poorly sampled neoplasm.

rom.source: Milan 2nd ed (Rossi et al., Cancer Cytopathol 2024, doi 10.1002/cncy.22753, Table 1)

categories.management: Repeat FNA or surgery (core biopsy an option); individualise with clinicoradiological correlation. Target AUS rate <10%. [Milan 2nd ed; Rossi et al. Cancer Cytopathol 2024 and review in IP Arch Cytol Histopathol Res]
criteria: Reactive/repair atypia or squamous/oncocytic metaplasia raising neoplasm.
Mucinous cyst contents with scant/no epithelium (low-grade MEC not excluded).
Scant aspirate with features suggestive but not diagnostic of neoplasm.
Atypical lymphoid population with insufficient material for flow.

diagnoses.name: AUS – mucinous cyst contents
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance (Milan Category III). Mucinous cyst contents with scant epithelial cells.
diagnoses.comment: Low-grade mucoepidermoid carcinoma cannot be excluded; repeat FNA of solid area/surgery and MAML2 testing if material allows.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System III – AUS

diagnoses.name: AUS – oncocytic/squamous metaplastic atypia
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance (Milan Category III). Atypical oncocytic/squamous metaplastic cells.
diagnoses.comment: Differential includes Warthin tumour with metaplasia, oncocytoma and neoplasm; repeat FNA suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System III – AUS

diagnoses.name: AUS – atypical lymphoid cells
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance (Milan Category III). Atypical lymphoid cells.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat FNA with flow cytometry.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System III – AUS

diagnoses.name: AUS – scant basaloid/epithelial cells
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance (Milan Category III). Scant atypical epithelial cells.
diagnoses.comment: Neoplasm cannot be excluded; repeat FNA or excision recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System III – AUS

categories.name: Neoplasm: Benign
categories.definition: Benign neoplasm diagnosed on well-established cytological criteria.

rom.source: Milan 2nd ed (Rossi et al., Cancer Cytopathol 2024, doi 10.1002/cncy.22753, Table 1)

categories.management: Surgery or clinical follow-up. [Milan 2nd ed; Rossi et al. Cancer Cytopathol 2024 and review in IP Arch Cytol Histopathol Res]
criteria: Pleomorphic adenoma: fibrillary chondromyxoid matrix (magenta on MGG) with embedded plasmacytoid/spindle myoepithelial cells.
Warthin tumour: oncocytic sheets, lymphocytes, granular/'dirty' proteinaceous background.
Lipoma, schwannoma, haemangioma, others with classic features.

diagnoses.name: Pleomorphic adenoma
diagnoses.final: Neoplasm: Benign (Milan Category IVA). Pleomorphic adenoma.
diagnoses.comment: Fibrillary chondromyxoid stroma with myoepithelial and ductal cells. Surgical excision recommended (risk of recurrence and rare malignant transformation).
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System IVA – Benign neoplasm

diagnoses.name: Warthin tumour
diagnoses.final: Neoplasm: Benign (Milan Category IVA). Warthin tumour.
diagnoses.comment: Flat sheets of oncocytic cells, background lymphocytes and granular cyst debris. Conservative management or excision according to clinical setting.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System IVA – Benign neoplasm

diagnoses.name: Lipoma
diagnoses.final: Neoplasm: Benign (Milan Category IVA). Lipoma.
diagnoses.comment: Mature adipocytes, concordant with imaging.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System IVA – Benign neoplasm

diagnoses.name: Schwannoma
diagnoses.final: Neoplasm: Benign (Milan Category IVA). Schwannoma.
diagnoses.comment: Spindle cells with wavy nuclei, Verocay-like fibrillary fragments; S100/SOX10+.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System IVA – Benign neoplasm

diagnoses.name: Haemangioma / lymphangioma
diagnoses.final: Neoplasm: Benign (Milan Category IVA). Vascular lesion consistent with haemangioma.
diagnoses.comment: Correlate with imaging.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System IVA – Benign neoplasm

diagnoses.name: Oncocytoma (classic, with clinical/imaging support)
diagnoses.final: Neoplasm: Benign (Milan Category IVA) – oncocytic neoplasm favouring oncocytoma; or classify as SUMP (IVB) if uncertain.
diagnoses.comment: Pure oncocytic aspirate; differential with Warthin, oncocytic MEC and acinic cell carcinoma.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System IVA/IVB

categories.name: Neoplasm: Salivary gland neoplasm of uncertain malignant potential (SUMP)
categories.definition: Neoplasm in which a benign neoplasm cannot be distinguished from a malignant one (e.g. cellular basaloid, oncocytic/oncocytoid, clear cell, atypical pleomorphic adenoma patterns).

rom.source: Milan 2nd ed (Rossi et al., Cancer Cytopathol 2024, doi 10.1002/cncy.22753, Table 1)

categories.management: Surgery (conservative/nerve-sparing); intraoperative consultation may guide extent. [Milan 2nd ed; Rossi et al. Cancer Cytopathol 2024 and review in IP Arch Cytol Histopathol Res]
criteria: Cellular basaloid neoplasm (basal cell adenoma vs adenoid cystic, basal cell adenocarcinoma, cellular PA).
Cellular oncocytic/oncocytoid neoplasm (oncocytoma vs MEC vs acinic cell/secretory carcinoma).
Clear cell neoplasm; cellular myoepithelial neoplasm; PA with atypical features.
Use subtyping descriptors and give differential diagnosis.

diagnoses.name: SUMP – basaloid neoplasm
diagnoses.final: Salivary gland neoplasm of uncertain malignant potential (Milan Category IVB) – basaloid neoplasm.
diagnoses.comment: Differential includes basal cell adenoma, cellular pleomorphic adenoma, adenoid cystic carcinoma and basal cell adenocarcinoma. MYB/PLAG1/HMGA2/β-catenin studies may help; excision recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System IVB – SUMP

diagnoses.name: SUMP – oncocytic/oncocytoid neoplasm
diagnoses.final: Salivary gland neoplasm of uncertain malignant potential (Milan Category IVB) – oncocytic/oncocytoid neoplasm.
diagnoses.comment: Differential: oncocytoma, Warthin, oncocytic MEC, acinic cell and secretory carcinoma. Excision recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System IVB – SUMP

diagnoses.name: SUMP – clear cell neoplasm
diagnoses.final: Salivary gland neoplasm of uncertain malignant potential (Milan Category IVB) – clear cell neoplasm.
diagnoses.comment: Differential includes myoepithelial neoplasm, clear cell carcinoma, epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma and metastatic RCC.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System IVB – SUMP

diagnoses.name: SUMP – myoepithelial neoplasm / cellular pleomorphic adenoma with atypia
diagnoses.final: Salivary gland neoplasm of uncertain malignant potential (Milan Category IVB) – myoepithelial-rich neoplasm.
diagnoses.comment: Myoepithelioma vs myoepithelial carcinoma; excision recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System IVB – SUMP

categories.name: Suspicious for malignancy
categories.definition: Features highly suggestive of malignancy but not definitive.

rom.source: Milan 2nd ed (Rossi et al., Cancer Cytopathol 2024, doi 10.1002/cncy.22753, Table 1)

categories.management: Surgery; intraoperative consultation to determine extent. [Milan 2nd ed; Rossi et al. Cancer Cytopathol 2024 and review in IP Arch Cytol Histopathol Res]
criteria: Atypical cells suspicious for high-grade carcinoma but scant/obscured.
Suspicious for specific types (e.g. adenoid cystic, MEC, lymphoma).

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for malignancy – carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy (Milan Category V). Suspicious for carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Surgery recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System V – Suspicious

diagnoses.name: Suspicious – adenoid cystic carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy (Milan Category V). Suspicious for adenoid cystic carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Basaloid cells with hyaline globules; MYB IHC/FISH can support.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System V – Suspicious

diagnoses.name: Suspicious – lymphoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy (Milan Category V). Suspicious for lymphoma.
diagnoses.comment: Flow cytometry/biopsy.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System V – Suspicious

categories.name: Malignant
categories.definition: Malignancy diagnosed; specify type and grade (2nd ed: low-grade vs high-grade).

rom.source: Milan 2nd ed (Rossi et al., Cancer Cytopathol 2024, doi 10.1002/cncy.22753, Table 1)

categories.management: Surgery; extent guided by low- vs high-grade (intraoperative consultation may help). [Milan 2nd ed; Rossi et al. Cancer Cytopathol 2024 and review in IP Arch Cytol Histopathol Res]
criteria: Low-grade: acinic cell, secretory, low-grade MEC, polymorphous adenocarcinoma, epithelial-myoepithelial, basal cell adenocarcinoma, intercalated duct-type.
High-grade: salivary duct carcinoma, high-grade MEC, adenoid cystic (solid), carcinoma ex PA, myoepithelial carcinoma (high-grade), SCC, lymphoepithelial carcinoma, metastases.

diagnoses.name: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma, low grade
diagnoses.final: Malignant (Milan Category VI) – low-grade carcinoma: mucoepidermoid carcinoma, low grade.
diagnoses.comment: Mucin, mucocytes, intermediate and squamoid cells; MAML2 rearrangement supports.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System VI – Malignant (low grade)

diagnoses.name: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma, high grade
diagnoses.final: Malignant (Milan Category VI) – high-grade carcinoma: mucoepidermoid carcinoma, high grade.
diagnoses.comment: High-grade MEC overlaps with salivary duct carcinoma and metastatic SCC; mucocytes may be scant. MAML2 rearrangement supports MEC. Classify as 'high-grade carcinoma' if subtyping not possible.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System VI – Malignant (high grade)

diagnoses.name: Acinic cell carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (Milan Category VI) – low-grade carcinoma: acinic cell carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Acinar cells with granular/vacuolated cytoplasm, lack of ducts/fat; NR4A3 IHC +, DOG1+.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System VI – Malignant (low grade)

diagnoses.name: Secretory carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (Milan Category VI) – low-grade carcinoma: secretory carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Vacuolated cells, mammaglobin/S100+, ETV6::NTRK3 fusion (pan-TRK IHC).
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System VI – Malignant (low grade)

diagnoses.name: Adenoid cystic carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (Milan Category VI) – adenoid cystic carcinoma (grade by solid component).
