diagnoses.comment: Basaloid cells around hyaline globules; MYB::NFIB fusion.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Polymorphous adenocarcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (Milan Category VI) – low-grade carcinoma: polymorphous adenocarcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Mostly minor glands; PRKD1 alterations.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System VI – Malignant (low grade)

diagnoses.name: Epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (Milan Category VI) – low-grade carcinoma: epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Biphasic: inner ductal (CK7+) and outer clear myoepithelial (p63/SOX10+) cells, often with basement-membrane hyaline globules; overlaps with pleomorphic adenoma and adenoid cystic carcinoma. Often low-grade; subtype confirmation on histology.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System VI – Malignant (low grade)

diagnoses.name: Salivary duct carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (Milan Category VI) – high-grade carcinoma: salivary duct carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Apocrine high-grade cells, necrosis; AR+, HER2 testing recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System VI – Malignant (high grade)

diagnoses.name: Carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (Milan Category VI) – carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma.
diagnoses.comment: Malignant component with residual PA matrix.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Myoepithelial carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (Milan Category VI) – myoepithelial carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Cytologically monotonous myoepithelial cells cannot be separated from myoepithelioma on FNA unless overt atypia/necrosis; diagnosis rests on invasion at histology – consider SUMP if atypia is mild.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Basal cell adenocarcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (Milan Category VI) – low-grade carcinoma: basal cell adenocarcinoma (usually requires histology; often SUMP on FNA).
diagnoses.comment: Basaloid cells with basement-membrane material indistinguishable from basal cell adenoma on cytology (invasion needed); usually reported as basaloid neoplasm, SUMP, unless clear malignant features.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System VI – Malignant (low grade)

diagnoses.name: Squamous cell carcinoma (usually metastatic)
diagnoses.final: Malignant (Milan Category VI) – squamous cell carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Primary salivary SCC is rare; exclude metastasis from skin/head and neck.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System VI – Malignant (high grade)

diagnoses.name: Lymphoma (MALT, DLBCL, etc.)
diagnoses.final: Malignant (Milan Category VI) – non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
diagnoses.comment: Flow cytometry/IHC.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Metastatic malignancy (melanoma, SCC skin, others)
diagnoses.final: Malignant (Milan Category VI) – metastatic [type].
diagnoses.comment: Intraparotid node metastases (cutaneous SCC, melanoma of head and neck) are common in older patients; correlate with skin cancer history; IHC (p40, SOX10/HMB45) on cell block.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Carcinoma, NOS / poorly differentiated
diagnoses.final: Malignant (Milan Category VI) – high-grade carcinoma, NOS.
diagnoses.comment: Use when malignant epithelial cells cannot be subtyped; exclude metastasis (lung, skin) and lymphoma; AR/GATA3/HER2 help for salivary duct carcinoma.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Milan System VI – Malignant (high grade)

references: Faquin WC, Rossi ED, et al. (eds). The Milan System for Reporting Salivary Gland Cytopathology. 2nd ed. Springer, 2023.
WHO Classification of Tumours Editorial Board. Head and Neck Tumours. 5th ed. IARC, 2022.

systems.name: The Paris System for Reporting Urinary Cytology (TPS)
systems.specimen: Voided and instrumented urine, bladder washings, upper-tract specimens
use: Lower and upper urinary tract cytology: voided, catheterised, bladder wash, upper-tract washings/brushings.
Primary purpose: detection of high-grade urothelial carcinoma.
not_use: Not designed to detect low-grade urothelial neoplasms (low sensitivity).
Non-urothelial lesions primarily (renal mass FNA – use kidney system).

adequacy.title: Adequacy
items: Voided: ≥25 mL (ThinPrep) or ≥30 mL (SurePath) recommended volume.
Instrumented: ≈20 well-visualised urothelial cells per 10 HPF (ThinPrep) as guidance.
Upper tract: lower thresholds acceptable.
Any atypical or worse cells → adequate.

categories.name: Non-diagnostic / Unsatisfactory
categories.definition: Specimen inadequate for evaluation of high-grade urothelial carcinoma.

rom.source: TPS 2.0 book (Springer 2022) via JCTP 2022 review Table 1
Pooled meta-analysis 'The Paris System for Reporting Urinary Cytology: A Meta-Analysis' (PMC8874476)

categories.management: Repeat urine cytology (preferably a fresh voided or instrumented sample); cystoscopy as clinically indicated.
criteria: Voided urine: volume below ~25–30 mL is suboptimal; very low cellularity.
Instrumented: fewer than ~20 urothelial cells/10 HPF (ThinPrep guidance).
Obscuring blood/inflammation/lubricant, degeneration.
Any atypical/suspicious/HGUC cells make the sample adequate.

diagnoses.name: Non-diagnostic – scant cellularity
diagnoses.final: Unsatisfactory/Non-diagnostic for evaluation of high-grade urothelial carcinoma – scant cellularity.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat urine sample (≥25–30 mL, fresh, ideally not first morning) recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – Non-diagnostic

diagnoses.name: Non-diagnostic – obscuring blood/degeneration
diagnoses.final: Unsatisfactory/Non-diagnostic – cellular detail obscured by blood/degeneration.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat fresh specimen recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – Non-diagnostic

categories.name: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma
categories.definition: Benign urothelial, squamous and glandular cells, reactive changes, LGUN-type groups without atypia, and benign findings.

rom.source: TPS 2.0 book (Springer 2022) via JCTP 2022 review Table 1
Pooled meta-analysis 'The Paris System for Reporting Urinary Cytology: A Meta-Analysis' (PMC8874476)

categories.management: Routine clinical follow-up/surveillance as indicated.
criteria: Benign urothelial cells, umbrella cells, benign urothelial tissue fragments and groups (incl. from instrumentation/stones).
Reactive/degenerated cells, polyoma (decoy) cells, treatment effects (BCG, chemo), ileal conduit cells.
N:C ratio <0.5 in non-superficial cells (TPS 2.0 AUC threshold >0.5).

diagnoses.name: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (NHGUC).
diagnoses.comment: Benign urothelial cells are seen.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – NHGUC

diagnoses.name: Benign urothelial tissue fragments / groups
diagnoses.final: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (NHGUC). Benign urothelial tissue fragments present.
diagnoses.comment: Seen with instrumentation, stones or low-grade neoplasia; not diagnostic of LGUN without cystoscopic lesion.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – NHGUC

diagnoses.name: Polyomavirus (BK) cytopathic effect (decoy cells)
diagnoses.final: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (NHGUC). Polyomavirus cytopathic effect present.
diagnoses.comment: Decoy cells with ground-glass intranuclear inclusions; in transplant patients consider BK viral load testing.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – NHGUC

diagnoses.name: Reactive urothelial cells (lithiasis, catheter, infection)
diagnoses.final: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (NHGUC). Reactive urothelial changes.
diagnoses.comment: Clinical correlation recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – NHGUC

diagnoses.name: Treatment effect (BCG, intravesical chemotherapy, radiation)
diagnoses.final: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (NHGUC). Changes consistent with therapy effect.
diagnoses.comment: BCG may show granulomas; mitomycin/radiation cause enlarged cells with preserved N:C ratio.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – NHGUC

diagnoses.name: Ileal conduit / neobladder urine
diagnoses.final: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (NHGUC). Degenerated enteric-type cells consistent with conduit urine.
diagnoses.comment: Clinical correlation recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – NHGUC

diagnoses.name: Squamous cells / organisms (Trichomonas, Schistosoma, fungi)
diagnoses.final: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (NHGUC). [Squamous cells / organism] noted.
diagnoses.comment: Schistosoma haematobium ova increase SCC risk.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – NHGUC

diagnoses.name: Low-grade urothelial neoplasm (second-line diagnosis)
diagnoses.final: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (NHGUC). Findings may represent a low-grade urothelial neoplasm (LGUN) [only with fibrovascular cores or a known cystoscopic lesion].
diagnoses.comment: In TPS 2.0 LGUN is no longer a separate primary category; it is reported as a second-line diagnosis under NHGUC. Cystoscopic/histological correlation. Reported ROHM for LGUN 0–44% (TPS 2.0 table, via JCTP 2022 review); pooled 12.5% (PMC8874476).
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – NHGUC

diagnoses.name: Seminal vesicle cells
diagnoses.final: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (NHGUC). Seminal vesicle cells present.
diagnoses.comment: Lipofuscin-containing atypical-looking cells; benign.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – NHGUC

categories.name: Atypical urothelial cells
categories.definition: Non-superficial, non-degenerated urothelial cells with N:C ratio >0.5 AND one of: hyperchromasia, irregular nuclear membranes, irregular coarse chromatin.

rom.source: TPS 2.0 book (Springer 2022) via JCTP 2022 review Table 1
Pooled meta-analysis 'The Paris System for Reporting Urinary Cytology: A Meta-Analysis' (PMC8874476)

categories.management: Repeat cytology, cystoscopy ± biopsy, ancillary tests (UroVysion FISH) where available; expected AUC rate 5–15% (TPS 2.0).
criteria: Required: N:C ratio >0.5 (moderately increased).
Plus one of: nuclear hyperchromasia (vs umbrella cells), irregular nuclear contours, irregular coarse clumped chromatin.
Do not use for degenerated cells or reactive changes alone.

diagnoses.name: Atypical urothelial cells
diagnoses.final: Atypical urothelial cells (AUC).
diagnoses.comment: Rare urothelial cells with increased N:C ratio and hyperchromasia are seen, insufficient for suspicious for HGUC. Cystoscopy/repeat cytology suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – AUC

categories.name: Suspicious for high-grade urothelial carcinoma
categories.definition: Urothelial cells with N:C ≥0.7 and moderate–severe hyperchromasia plus at least one of irregular membranes or coarse chromatin, but fewer than the threshold for HGUC.

rom.source: TPS 2.0 book (Springer 2022) via JCTP 2022 review Table 1
Pooled meta-analysis 'The Paris System for Reporting Urinary Cytology: A Meta-Analysis' (PMC8874476)

categories.management: Cystoscopy with biopsy; upper tract evaluation if bladder negative.
criteria: Required: N:C ratio ≥0.7 and moderate to severe hyperchromasia.
Plus one of: markedly irregular nuclear membranes or coarse/clumped chromatin.
Number of such cells below HGUC threshold (<5–10 in voided).

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for high-grade urothelial carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (SHGUC).
diagnoses.comment: Few cells with high N:C ratio and hyperchromasia; cystoscopy with biopsy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – SHGUC

categories.name: High-grade urothelial carcinoma
categories.definition: Includes invasive HGUC and urothelial carcinoma in situ; ≥5–10 cells meeting criteria.

rom.source: TPS 2.0 book (Springer 2022) via JCTP 2022 review Table 1
Pooled meta-analysis 'The Paris System for Reporting Urinary Cytology: A Meta-Analysis' (PMC8874476)

categories.management: Cystoscopy, biopsy/TURBT, upper tract imaging.
criteria: N:C ≥0.7, moderate–severe hyperchromasia, markedly irregular nuclear membranes, coarse clumped chromatin.
Cellular pleomorphism, single cells, necrosis, mitoses; minimum ~5–10 abnormal cells in voided specimens.
Variants (squamous/glandular differentiation, micropapillary, plasmacytoid) may be mentioned.

diagnoses.name: High-grade urothelial carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Positive for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (HGUC).
diagnoses.comment: Cystoscopy with biopsy and upper urinary tract evaluation recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – HGUC

diagnoses.name: High-grade urothelial carcinoma with squamous/glandular differentiation
diagnoses.final: Positive for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (HGUC), with squamous differentiation.
diagnoses.comment: Clinical correlation recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – HGUC

diagnoses.name: High-grade urothelial carcinoma, micropapillary/plasmacytoid features
diagnoses.final: Positive for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (HGUC) with [micropapillary / plasmacytoid] features.
diagnoses.comment: Aggressive subtypes; histological confirmation required.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – HGUC

diagnoses.name: Urothelial carcinoma in situ (cytologic correlate)
diagnoses.final: Positive for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (HGUC).
diagnoses.comment: Cytology cannot distinguish CIS from invasive HGUC; cystoscopy and biopsy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – HGUC

criteria: Primary: squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma (incl. urachal), small cell carcinoma, sarcoma.
Secondary: prostate, colorectal, cervical, renal cell carcinoma, lymphoma, melanoma.

diagnoses.final: Positive for malignancy – adenocarcinoma.

diagnoses.final: Positive for malignancy – small cell (high-grade neuroendocrine) carcinoma.

extra.title: Changes in TPS 2.0
items: LGUN removed as a primary category – now a second-line diagnosis within NHGUC.
AUC: N:C 0.5–0.7 plus one minor criterion; expected AUC rate 5–15%.
'Atypical urothelial cells' requires one secondary feature (hyperchromasia, irregular membranes, or coarse chromatin).
LGUN and NHGUC clarified; upper tract and ileal conduit chapters; ancillary tests chapter.

The Paris System for Reporting Urinary Cytology: A Meta-Analysis (PMC8874476).

systems.name: The International System for Reporting Serous Fluid Cytopathology (TIS / ISRSFC)
systems.specimen: Pleural, peritoneal (ascitic), pericardial fluids and peritoneal washings
use: Pleural, peritoneal and pericardial effusions.
Peritoneal washings can be reported using these categories, with staging context (TIS includes a washing chapter).
not_use: CSF, synovial fluid, cyst fluids, BAL (report descriptively/other systems).
Urine (use Paris System).
Do not use to diagnose mesothelioma without ancillary support.
report_structure: Ancillary results (IHC on cell block, flow, FISH)

adequacy.title: Volume and processing
items: Minimum 50–75 mL recommended for pleural fluid; larger volumes do not further increase sensitivity substantially.
Fresh specimen or refrigerated at 4 °C if delayed (stable up to ~2 weeks); no fixative needed.
Prepare cytospin/smears + cell block routinely for ancillary testing.
No numeric cellularity threshold – adequacy is a judgement; presence of mesothelial cells/macrophages confirms sampling of the space.

categories.name: Non-diagnostic
categories.definition: Insufficient cellular material for interpretation (e.g. acellular, only blood, degenerated/obscured cells). Very rare in serous fluids.

rom.source: TIS book 2020 (figures derived from Farahani & Baloch, Diagn Cytopathol 2019, doi 10.1002/dc.24278: 17.4/20.7/65.9/81.8/98.9%)
Meta-analysis, 16 studies/19,128 cases (Cancer Cytopathol 2024, doi 10.1002/cncy.22822) – pooled (95% CI)
Meta-analysis, 16 studies (Jamal, Vey et al., 2024) – pooled (95% CI)

categories.management: Repeat analysis if clinical suspicion persists; ensure adequate volume (≥75 mL) and fresh/refrigerated specimen.
criteria: Acellular or paucicellular specimen with no mesothelial cells/macrophages (sampling of wrong space).
Marked degeneration, drying, or obscuring blood precluding evaluation.
Use only after excluding processing issues; a few benign cells generally qualify as NFM.

diagnoses.name: Non-diagnostic – acellular/insufficient
diagnoses.final: Non-diagnostic. The specimen is acellular/insufficient for cytological evaluation.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat sampling with adequate volume (≥75 mL suggested for pleural fluid) is recommended if clinically indicated.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: ND (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Non-diagnostic – degenerated/obscured
diagnoses.final: Non-diagnostic. Cells are poorly preserved/obscured by blood.
diagnoses.comment: Send fresh specimen promptly or refrigerated (4 °C) for repeat analysis.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: ND (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

categories.name: Negative for malignancy
categories.definition: Benign/reactive elements only, with or without specific benign findings.

rom.source: TIS book 2020 (figures derived from Farahani & Baloch, Diagn Cytopathol 2019, doi 10.1002/dc.24278: 17.4/20.7/65.9/81.8/98.9%)
Meta-analysis, 16 studies/19,128 cases (Cancer Cytopathol 2024, doi 10.1002/cncy.22822) – pooled (95% CI)
Meta-analysis, 16 studies (Jamal, Vey et al., 2024) – pooled (95% CI)

categories.management: Clinical follow-up; investigate cause of effusion. Repeat cytology if suspicion of malignancy remains.
criteria: Reactive mesothelial cells (singly, small groups, 'windows', two-tone cytoplasm, binucleation), macrophages, inflammatory cells.
Specific benign entities may be named (e.g. lymphocytic, eosinophilic, LE cells, rheumatoid pattern, organisms).
No population of 'foreign' cells; second population absent.

diagnoses.name: Reactive mesothelial cells, macrophages and inflammatory cells
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. Reactive mesothelial cells, macrophages and mixed inflammatory cells.
diagnoses.comment: No malignant cells seen. Correlate clinically.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Lymphocyte-rich effusion (e.g. tuberculosis, post-CABG, chronic)
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. Lymphocyte-rich effusion.
diagnoses.comment: Predominantly small mature lymphocytes. Consider tuberculosis (ADA, GeneXpert/culture); if monotonous or atypical, flow cytometry to exclude lymphoma.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Eosinophilic effusion (>10% eosinophils)
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. Eosinophilic effusion.
diagnoses.comment: Often associated with air/blood in pleural space (pneumothorax, trauma, prior tap), drugs, parasites, Churg–Strauss. Clinical correlation advised.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Neutrophil-rich/suppurative effusion (empyema, parapneumonic)
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. Acute inflammatory (neutrophil-rich) effusion.
diagnoses.comment: Suggest culture and biochemical correlation (pH, glucose, LDH).
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Rheumatoid pleuritis pattern
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. Features consistent with rheumatoid pleuritis.
diagnoses.comment: Elongated/spindle histiocytes, multinucleated giant cells and granular necrotic background; correlate with rheumatoid serology.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Lupus pleuritis (LE cells)
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. LE cells identified; findings compatible with lupus serositis in proper clinical setting.
diagnoses.comment: Correlate with ANA/anti-dsDNA.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Endometriosis
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. Findings may represent endometriosis (haemosiderin-laden macrophages ± endometrial-type cells).
diagnoses.comment: Clinical correlation recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Organisms / infection (fungi, parasites, e.g. Strongyloides, microfilaria)
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. [Organism] identified.
diagnoses.comment: Clinical correlation and microbiological confirmation recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Benign elements – peritoneal washing (Müllerian/endosalpingiosis, benign mesothelium)
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. Benign mesothelial cells (± benign Müllerian-type epithelium/endosalpingiosis with psammoma bodies).
diagnoses.comment: Peritoneal washings with endosalpingiosis can mimic serous neoplasia; correlate with histology.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Contaminants (skin squames, cartilage, hepatocytes, bowel content)
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. Sampling contaminants noted.
diagnoses.comment: Contaminants related to sampling path; bowel contents may indicate inadvertent bowel puncture/perforation – inform clinician.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Extramedullary haematopoiesis / megakaryocytes
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. Extramedullary haematopoiesis present.
diagnoses.comment: Seen in myelofibrosis or contamination by bone marrow; correlate clinically.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

categories.name: Atypia of undetermined significance
categories.definition: Cells with atypia insufficient for SFM or MAL, most often reactive mesothelial atypia vs well-differentiated malignancy that cannot be resolved.

rom.source: TIS book 2020 (figures derived from Farahani & Baloch, Diagn Cytopathol 2019, doi 10.1002/dc.24278: 17.4/20.7/65.9/81.8/98.9%)
Meta-analysis, 16 studies/19,128 cases (Cancer Cytopathol 2024, doi 10.1002/cncy.22822) – pooled (95% CI)
Meta-analysis, 16 studies (Jamal, Vey et al., 2024) – pooled (95% CI)

categories.management: Repeat cytology with ancillary tests (cell block IHC: calretinin/WT1/D2-40 vs Ber-EP4/MOC-31/Claudin-4; BAP1, MTAP, CDKN2A FISH); clinical/radiological correlation. Lab AUS rate ideally <10%.
criteria: Mild–moderate nuclear atypia in a few cells, especially in presence of inflammation/ascites of cirrhosis.
Atypical lymphoid cells with insufficient material for flow cytometry.
Ancillary testing not done/inconclusive.
Avoid as a 'wastebasket'; explain the reason for atypia in the comment.

diagnoses.name: AUS – atypical mesothelial cells (reactive vs neoplastic)
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance. Atypical mesothelial cells present.
diagnoses.comment: Reactive mesothelial atypia vs mesothelioma cannot be distinguished on this material. Suggest repeat sampling with cell block for BAP1/MTAP IHC and clinico-radiological correlation.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: AUS (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: AUS – atypical epithelioid cells, few
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance. Few atypical epithelioid cells of uncertain nature.
diagnoses.comment: Insufficient for further characterisation; repeat fluid with cell block for IHC suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: AUS (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: AUS – atypical lymphoid cells
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance. Atypical lymphoid population.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat sample with flow cytometry recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: AUS (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

categories.name: Suspicious for malignancy
categories.definition: Features strongly suggestive of malignancy but quantitatively/qualitatively insufficient, or ancillary studies not available/confirmatory.

rom.source: TIS book 2020 (figures derived from Farahani & Baloch, Diagn Cytopathol 2019, doi 10.1002/dc.24278: 17.4/20.7/65.9/81.8/98.9%)
Meta-analysis, 16 studies/19,128 cases (Cancer Cytopathol 2024, doi 10.1002/cncy.22822) – pooled (95% CI)
Meta-analysis, 16 studies (Jamal, Vey et al., 2024) – pooled (95% CI)

categories.management: Ancillary studies on cell block/additional fluid; tissue biopsy (pleural biopsy/thoracoscopy) as needed.
criteria: Few highly atypical cells or second population suspicious for carcinoma.
Atypical mesothelial proliferation suspicious for mesothelioma without confirmatory BAP1/MTAP loss or CDKN2A deletion.
Lymphoid population suspicious for lymphoma without flow/IHC confirmation.

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for metastatic carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy – suspicious for metastatic carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: A small population of atypical epithelial cells suspicious for carcinoma is present; IHC on cell block/repeat sample recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: SFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for mesothelioma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy – atypical mesothelial proliferation, suspicious for mesothelioma.
diagnoses.comment: Recommend BAP1/MTAP IHC and/or CDKN2A FISH, and tissue correlation (pleural biopsy).
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: SFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for lymphoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy – suspicious for lymphoma.
diagnoses.comment: Flow cytometry and IHC on cell block recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: SFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

categories.name: Malignant (primary or secondary)
categories.definition: Unequivocal malignancy. Primary: mesothelioma, primary effusion lymphoma. Secondary: metastatic carcinoma, lymphoma/leukaemia, melanoma, sarcoma, germ cell tumours, etc.

rom.source: TIS book 2020 (figures derived from Farahani & Baloch, Diagn Cytopathol 2019, doi 10.1002/dc.24278: 17.4/20.7/65.9/81.8/98.9%)
Meta-analysis, 16 studies/19,128 cases (Cancer Cytopathol 2024, doi 10.1002/cncy.22822) – pooled (95% CI)
Meta-analysis, 16 studies (Jamal, Vey et al., 2024) – pooled (95% CI)

categories.management: Oncology referral. Use cell block for IHC/predictive biomarkers (e.g. ER/PR/HER2, EGFR/ALK/PD-L1, MMR).
criteria: Metastatic adenocarcinoma: second 'foreign' population, 3-D 'cannonball'/papillary/acinar clusters, cytoplasmic vacuoles, signet-ring cells; MOC-31/Ber-EP4/Claudin-4+.
Mesothelioma: numerous mesothelial cells, large morula-like groups with knobby borders, cell-in-cell, macronucleoli; confirm with loss of BAP1/MTAP or CDKN2A homozygous deletion.
Lymphoma: monotonous dispersed lymphoid cells, lymphoglandular bodies; flow cytometry.
Squamous carcinoma, small cell carcinoma, melanoma, sarcoma, germ cell tumour.

diagnoses.name: Metastatic adenocarcinoma (specify likely primary)
diagnoses.final: Malignant – secondary: Metastatic adenocarcinoma, [IHC profile consistent with primary in lung/breast/ovary/GI tract].
diagnoses.comment: IHC on cell block: [list]. Predictive biomarkers can be performed on the cell block if requested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Secondary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Metastatic breast carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant – secondary: Metastatic carcinoma, consistent with breast primary (GATA3+, ER+).
diagnoses.comment: ER/PR/HER2 can be done on the cell block.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Secondary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Metastatic lung adenocarcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant – secondary: Metastatic adenocarcinoma, consistent with lung primary (TTF1+, Napsin A+).
diagnoses.comment: Cell block suitable for EGFR/ALK/ROS1/PD-L1 testing.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Secondary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Metastatic high-grade serous carcinoma (Müllerian)
diagnoses.final: Malignant – secondary: Metastatic high-grade serous carcinoma, consistent with Müllerian (tubo-ovarian/peritoneal) origin (PAX8+, WT1+, aberrant p53).
diagnoses.comment: Correlate with CA-125 and imaging.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Secondary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Metastatic gastrointestinal/pancreatobiliary adenocarcinoma (incl. signet-ring)
diagnoses.final: Malignant – secondary: Metastatic adenocarcinoma, consistent with GI/pancreatobiliary origin (CK20+, CDX2+, SATB2±).
diagnoses.comment: Correlate with endoscopy/imaging.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Secondary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Metastatic squamous cell carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant – secondary: Metastatic squamous cell carcinoma (p40+).
diagnoses.comment: Search for primary (lung, cervix, head and neck, oesophagus).
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Secondary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Metastatic small cell / neuroendocrine carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant – secondary: Metastatic small cell carcinoma (synaptophysin/INSM1+).
diagnoses.comment: Most commonly lung primary.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Secondary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Metastatic melanoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant – secondary: Metastatic melanoma (SOX10/S100/HMB45/Melan-A+).
diagnoses.comment: Melanin pigment may be absent (amelanotic); correlate with history of cutaneous/ocular melanoma. BRAF testing can be done on the cell block.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Secondary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Lymphoma/leukaemia involving effusion
diagnoses.final: Malignant – secondary: Involvement by [lymphoma type/leukaemia].
diagnoses.comment: Flow cytometry/IHC performed/recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Secondary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Metastatic sarcoma / germ cell tumour / other
diagnoses.final: Malignant – secondary: Metastatic [sarcoma/germ cell tumour].
diagnoses.comment: IHC and clinical correlation.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Secondary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Mesothelioma (epithelioid)
diagnoses.final: Malignant – primary: Malignant cells consistent with mesothelioma (epithelioid type).
diagnoses.comment: Mesothelial phenotype (calretinin/WT1/D2-40+, Claudin-4/MOC-31−) with BAP1 loss and/or MTAP loss/CDKN2A deletion. Clinico-radiological correlation recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Primary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Primary effusion lymphoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant – primary: Primary effusion lymphoma (HHV8+).
diagnoses.comment: Large plasmablastic/immunoblastic cells, CD45±, CD138+, HHV8 (LANA)+; usually HIV setting.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Primary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Fluid overload–associated large B-cell lymphoma (HHV8-negative)
diagnoses.final: Malignant – primary: Large B-cell lymphoma in effusion, HHV8-negative (fluid overload-associated large B-cell lymphoma).
diagnoses.comment: WHO-HAEM5 entity; usually elderly with fluid overload.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Primary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)
diagnoses.note: WHO-HAEM5 (2022) term; not in TIS 2020 book.

diagnoses.name: Well-differentiated papillary mesothelial tumour
diagnoses.final: Report descriptively – papillary mesothelial proliferation; not reliably diagnosed on fluid.
diagnoses.comment: Histology required.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: AUS/SFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

extra.title: Ancillary panels (cell block)
items: Mesothelial: calretinin, WT1, D2-40, CK5/6, HBME-1.
Epithelial (carcinoma): Claudin-4, MOC-31, Ber-EP4, B72.3, CEA.
Mesothelioma vs reactive: BAP1 loss, MTAP loss, CDKN2A (p16) FISH homozygous deletion; (desmin+ favours reactive, EMA membranous favours malignant – less reliable).
Site-specific: TTF1/Napsin (lung), GATA3/ER (breast), PAX8/WT1 (Müllerian), CDX2/CK20/SATB2 (GI), SOX10 (melanoma).

categories.management: MDT decides treatment. Suspicious axillary nodes: FNAB, then core if needed (may spare sentinel node procedure). Special-type carcinomas need excision for typing; cell block for ICC/biomarkers. [WHO book, paraphrased]
criteria: As Yokohama.

diagnoses.name: Invasive breast carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (WHO Breast System). Invasive breast carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: ER/PR/HER2 on core/cell block.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO Breast System – Malignant

extra.title: Status
items: Category names verified (same as Yokohama). ROM figures from the online beta chapter text; full diagnoses on the Yokohama page.

references: WHO Reporting System for Breast Cytopathology. IAC-IARC-WHO cytopathology reporting systems series, 1st ed., vol. 5. Lyon: IARC; 2026.
Field AS, Raymond WA, Schmitt F (eds). The International Academy of Cytology Yokohama System for Reporting Breast Fine Needle Aspiration Biopsy Cytopathology. Springer, 2020.

systems.name: The International Academy of Cytology Yokohama System for Reporting Breast Fine Needle Aspiration Biopsy Cytopathology
systems.specimen: Breast FNA (palpation or image-guided), including axillary tail lesions
use: All breast FNA specimens (palpable and image-guided).
Interpret alongside clinical examination and imaging (triple test).
Male breast lesions.
not_use: Nipple discharge and nipple scrape cytology (report descriptively).
Axillary lymph nodes (use Sydney system).
Core needle biopsy histology (use histological B-categories, e.g. UK B1–B5).
report_structure: Specimen, side, site (clock position), guidance, lesion size and imaging category (BI-RADS) if available
Comment: triple-test correlation and recommended next step
terminology: Use 'Carcinoma, consistent with ductal carcinoma NST' (or 'Malignant – carcinoma') on cytology; avoid 'invasive', 'infiltrating' and 'IDC' because invasion cannot be assessed on FNA.
DCIS cannot be distinguished from invasive carcinoma on FNA.

adequacy.title: Adequacy principles
items: No numerical threshold; adequacy depends on whether the material allows a confident diagnosis in the context of the clinical and imaging findings.
Rapid on-site evaluation (ROSE) reduces insufficient rates.
Specimens with atypical/suspicious/malignant cells are never 'Insufficient'.
Benign cyst fluid with resolution of cyst on imaging may be reported as Benign; fat alone is insufficient unless concordant with lipoma.

categories.name: Insufficient / Inadequate
categories.definition: Material is too scant, too poorly preserved or obscured to allow a cytological diagnosis; judged relative to the clinical/imaging lesion.

rom.source: Yokohama system (Field et al., Acta Cytol 2019;63:257, doi 10.1159/000499509) – range from two series
Pooled literature review (Acta Cytol 2019;63:292–301; 27 studies, 33,341 FNABs)

categories.management: Repeat FNA (preferably image-guided) or core needle biopsy, guided by triple-test (clinical + imaging) findings.
criteria: Insufficient epithelial cells for diagnosis in a solid lesion (no fixed number; experience-based judgement).
Poor fixation/air-drying, crush, thick smears, obscuring blood.
Cyst fluid with only macrophages and no epithelium – may be 'Benign' if imaging shows simple cyst that resolved; otherwise Insufficient.
Fat only from a mass lesion is insufficient unless clinically/radiologically a lipoma.

diagnoses.name: Insufficient – scant/acellular material
diagnoses.final: Insufficient/Inadequate (IAC Yokohama Category 1). The material is insufficient for cytological diagnosis.
diagnoses.comment: Correlate with clinical and imaging findings (triple test). Repeat image-guided FNA or core biopsy is recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 1 Insufficient

diagnoses.name: Insufficient – artefact/obscured
diagnoses.final: Insufficient/Inadequate (IAC Yokohama Category 1) due to air-drying/crush artefact/obscuring blood.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat FNA/core biopsy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 1 Insufficient

diagnoses.name: Insufficient – cyst fluid only (non-concordant imaging)
diagnoses.final: Insufficient/Inadequate (IAC Yokohama Category 1). Cyst contents with macrophages only; no epithelial cells.
diagnoses.comment: If imaging shows a complex cyst or residual mass, repeat FNA/core biopsy of the solid component is recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 1 Insufficient

categories.name: Benign
categories.definition: Clearly benign cytological features, with a specific diagnosis where possible.

rom.source: Yokohama system (Field et al., Acta Cytol 2019;63:257, doi 10.1159/000499509) – range from two series
Pooled literature review (Acta Cytol 2019;63:292–301; 27 studies, 33,341 FNABs)

categories.management: If triple test concordant benign: clinical/imaging follow-up. If not concordant: core biopsy.
criteria: Moderate cellularity of cohesive flat sheets of ductal cells with myoepithelial cells, bare bipolar nuclei in background.
Specific patterns: fibroadenoma (staghorn sheets, fibromyxoid stroma, bipolar nuclei), fat necrosis, mastitis, lactational change, cyst with apocrine cells, gynaecomastia.
No significant atypia, no dyscohesion beyond expected.

diagnoses.name: Fibroadenoma
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Consistent with fibroadenoma.
diagnoses.comment: Cellular aspirate with branching (staghorn) cohesive sheets with myoepithelial cells, numerous bare bipolar nuclei and fibromyxoid stromal fragments. Correlate with triple test.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 2 Benign

diagnoses.name: Fibrocystic change (incl. apocrine metaplasia, cyst)
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Fibrocystic change.
diagnoses.comment: Benign ductal cells, apocrine cells, foamy macrophages and cyst fluid.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 2 Benign

diagnoses.name: Benign cyst
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Consistent with benign cyst.
diagnoses.comment: Correlate with imaging; aspirate residual mass if present.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 2 Benign

diagnoses.name: Fat necrosis
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Consistent with fat necrosis.
diagnoses.comment: Foamy/lipid-laden macrophages, multinucleated giant cells and degenerated fat. History of trauma/surgery supports; correlate with imaging.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 2 Benign

diagnoses.name: Acute mastitis / breast abscess
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Acute inflammation/abscess.
diagnoses.comment: Neutrophils and debris; culture advised; follow up to resolution to exclude inflammatory carcinoma.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 2 Benign

diagnoses.name: Subareolar abscess / duct ectasia / periductal mastitis
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Features of subareolar abscess (anucleate squames, keratin, inflammation) / duct ectasia.
diagnoses.comment: Correlate clinically.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 2 Benign

diagnoses.name: Granulomatous mastitis (idiopathic/tuberculous)
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Granulomatous mastitis.
diagnoses.comment: Epithelioid granulomas ± necrosis. ZN stain/AFB culture/CBNAAT recommended to exclude tuberculosis; idiopathic granulomatous lobular mastitis in differential.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 2 Benign

diagnoses.name: Lactational change / lactating adenoma
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Lactational change.
diagnoses.comment: Cells with vacuolated cytoplasm, prominent nucleoli and proteinaceous background; pregnancy/lactation history required.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 2 Benign

diagnoses.name: Gynaecomastia
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Consistent with gynaecomastia.
diagnoses.comment: Cohesive ductal sheets with bipolar nuclei in a male breast.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 2 Benign

diagnoses.name: Intramammary lymph node
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Reactive lymphoid cells consistent with intramammary lymph node.
diagnoses.comment: Polymorphous lymphoid cells with tingible-body macrophages and no epithelial cells. Correlate with imaging (reniform node with fatty hilum).
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 2 Benign

diagnoses.name: Lipoma / benign adipose tissue (concordant)
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Mature adipose tissue, consistent with lipoma in the clinical/radiological context.
diagnoses.comment: Fat alone is considered Insufficient if imaging suggests a solid non-fatty lesion.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 2 Benign

diagnoses.name: Benign proliferative breast disease without atypia
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Proliferative breast disease without atypia.
diagnoses.comment: Cellular cohesive sheets with streaming and myoepithelial cells; usual ductal hyperplasia/papilloma may be within this pattern.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 2 Benign

diagnoses.name: Benign skin adnexal cyst (epidermal inclusion cyst)
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Contents of epidermal inclusion cyst.
diagnoses.comment: Anucleate squames and keratinous debris ± foreign-body giant cells; ruptured cysts can cause reactive atypia.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 2 Benign

diagnoses.name: Silicone/foreign-body reaction
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Foreign-body (silicone) reaction.
diagnoses.comment: Vacuolated histiocytes and giant cells with refractile non-birefringent material; correlate with implant history.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 2 Benign

categories.name: Atypical
categories.definition: Cytological features that are mainly benign but with some features seen uncommonly in benign lesions and that may be seen in malignancy; or features of a lesion with uncertain behaviour.

rom.source: Yokohama system (Field et al., Acta Cytol 2019;63:257, doi 10.1159/000499509) – range from two series
Pooled literature review (Acta Cytol 2019;63:292–301; 27 studies, 33,341 FNABs)

categories.management: Core needle biopsy (preferred) or repeat FNA; manage per triple test.
criteria: Benign pattern with mild atypia, loss of cohesion, or increased cellularity.
Papillary lesion without atypia (fibrovascular cores, columnar cells) – papilloma vs papillary carcinoma uncertain.
Fibroepithelial lesion with cellular stroma (fibroadenoma vs phyllodes).
Mucinous lesion with scant atypia (mucocele-like lesion vs mucinous carcinoma).
Columnar cell lesions/atypical ductal hyperplasia-like patterns; low cellularity atypical cells.

diagnoses.name: Atypical – papillary lesion
diagnoses.final: Atypical (IAC Yokohama Category 3). Papillary lesion.
diagnoses.comment: Papillary fragments with fibrovascular cores and columnar cells; papilloma cannot be distinguished from papillary carcinoma on cytology. Core biopsy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 3 Atypical

diagnoses.name: Atypical – fibroepithelial lesion with cellular stroma (fibroadenoma vs phyllodes)
diagnoses.final: Atypical (IAC Yokohama Category 3). Fibroepithelial lesion; phyllodes tumour cannot be excluded.
diagnoses.comment: Hypercellular stromal fragments with spindle cells. Core biopsy/excision recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 3 Atypical

diagnoses.name: Atypical – mucinous lesion
diagnoses.final: Atypical (IAC Yokohama Category 3). Mucinous lesion.
diagnoses.comment: Mucin with few bland epithelial cells; differential includes mucocele-like lesion and mucinous carcinoma. Core biopsy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 3 Atypical

diagnoses.name: Atypical – epithelial cells with mild atypia
diagnoses.final: Atypical (IAC Yokohama Category 3). Atypical ductal epithelial cells.
diagnoses.comment: Benign versus low-grade neoplasia (e.g. ADH/low-grade DCIS/low-grade carcinoma) cannot be resolved; core biopsy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 3 Atypical

diagnoses.name: Atypical – low cellularity with atypia
diagnoses.final: Atypical (IAC Yokohama Category 3). Few atypical cells.
diagnoses.comment: Insufficient for a definite diagnosis; repeat FNA/core biopsy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 3 Atypical

diagnoses.name: Atypical – atypical apocrine cells
diagnoses.final: Atypical (IAC Yokohama Category 3). Atypical apocrine cells.
diagnoses.comment: Apocrine atypia may be reactive (e.g. in sclerosing adenosis) or neoplastic; core biopsy suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 3 Atypical

diagnoses.name: Atypical – granular cell tumour / spindle cell lesion
diagnoses.final: Atypical (IAC Yokohama Category 3). Spindle cell lesion / granular cells.
diagnoses.comment: Includes granular cell tumour, myofibroblastoma, fibromatosis, nodular fasciitis; core biopsy for IHC.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 3 Atypical

diagnoses.name: Atypical – radial scar/complex sclerosing lesion pattern
diagnoses.final: Atypical (IAC Yokohama Category 3).
diagnoses.comment: Cytology cannot reliably distinguish from tubular carcinoma; core biopsy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 3 Atypical

categories.name: Suspicious of malignancy
categories.definition: Features suggestive of, but not diagnostic of, malignancy (quantity or quality insufficient), or specific lesions where only histology can confirm.

rom.source: Yokohama system (Field et al., Acta Cytol 2019;63:257, doi 10.1159/000499509) – range from two series
Pooled literature review (Acta Cytol 2019;63:292–301; 27 studies, 33,341 FNABs)

categories.management: Core needle biopsy (or excision) before definitive treatment.
criteria: Low cellularity with malignant-appearing cells.
Moderate atypia in a dyscohesive population lacking myoepithelial cells, but insufficient for malignancy.
Suspicious of low-grade carcinoma (lobular, tubular, low-grade NST).
Poorly preserved/obscured atypical cells.

diagnoses.name: Suspicious of malignancy – carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious of malignancy (IAC Yokohama Category 4). Suspicious of carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Atypical dyscohesive epithelial cells, quantitatively/qualitatively insufficient for a definitive malignant diagnosis. Core biopsy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 4 Suspicious

diagnoses.name: Suspicious – lobular carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious of malignancy (IAC Yokohama Category 4). Suspicious of lobular carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Small monotonous single cells/linear files with intracytoplasmic lumina; core biopsy with E-cadherin recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 4 Suspicious

diagnoses.name: Suspicious – low-grade/tubular carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious of malignancy (IAC Yokohama Category 4). Suspicious of low-grade carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Angular tubules with minimal atypia and absent myoepithelial cells. Core biopsy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 4 Suspicious

diagnoses.name: Suspicious – papillary carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious of malignancy (IAC Yokohama Category 4). Papillary lesion, suspicious of papillary carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Core biopsy/excision recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 4 Suspicious

diagnoses.name: Suspicious – mucinous carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious of malignancy (IAC Yokohama Category 4). Mucinous lesion suspicious of mucinous carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Abundant mucin with atypical epithelial clusters but insufficient for definitive diagnosis; core biopsy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 4 Suspicious

categories.name: Malignant
categories.definition: Unequivocal malignant features; specify type where possible. Do not use 'invasive'/'infiltrating' on cytology because invasion cannot be assessed.

rom.source: Yokohama system (Field et al., Acta Cytol 2019;63:257, doi 10.1159/000499509) – range from two series
Pooled literature review (Acta Cytol 2019;63:292–301; 27 studies, 33,341 FNABs)

categories.management: If triple test concordant malignant: definitive management may proceed per local policy, but core biopsy is generally recommended for histological type, grade and biomarkers (ER/PR/HER2/Ki-67).
criteria: Usually cellular, dyscohesive population of atypical epithelial cells, absent bipolar nuclei/myoepithelial cells.
Nuclear enlargement, pleomorphism, irregular chromatin, nucleoli; necrosis in high-grade.
Specific types: lobular, mucinous, papillary, medullary-like, metaplastic, apocrine, secretory, adenoid cystic, lymphoma, metastasis, sarcoma/malignant phyllodes.

diagnoses.name: Carcinoma, consistent with ductal carcinoma NST
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Carcinoma, consistent with ductal carcinoma of no special type (NST).
diagnoses.comment: Cellular dyscohesive pleomorphic malignant epithelial cells with absent myoepithelial cells. In-situ versus invasive disease cannot be determined on cytology. Core biopsy for histological type, grade and ER/PR/HER2/Ki-67 is recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 5 Malignant

diagnoses.name: Lobular carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Carcinoma, consistent with lobular carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Dyscohesive small monotonous cells with intracytoplasmic lumina/signet-ring forms. Core biopsy with E-cadherin and biomarkers recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 5 Malignant

diagnoses.name: Mucinous carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Carcinoma, consistent with mucinous carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Abundant extracellular mucin with clusters of mildly atypical cells and capillary fragments.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 5 Malignant

diagnoses.name: Papillary carcinoma (encapsulated/solid/invasive)
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Papillary carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Histology needed to determine encapsulated/solid papillary or invasive status.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 5 Malignant

diagnoses.name: Carcinoma with medullary features / triple-negative high-grade
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). High-grade carcinoma (NST) with medullary-like features.
diagnoses.comment: Syncytial sheets of large pleomorphic cells with lymphocytes; biomarkers on core.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 5 Malignant

diagnoses.name: Metaplastic carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Malignant neoplasm, consistent with metaplastic carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Squamous/spindle/matrix-producing components; CK (incl. p63/CK5/6) on core needed.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 5 Malignant

diagnoses.name: Apocrine carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Carcinoma with apocrine features.
diagnoses.comment: AR+/GCDFP-15+ on core.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 5 Malignant

diagnoses.name: Secretory carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Carcinoma, consistent with secretory carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: ETV6::NTRK3 fusion; pan-TRK IHC on core.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 5 Malignant

diagnoses.name: Adenoid cystic carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Carcinoma consistent with adenoid cystic carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Basaloid cells with hyaline globules; MYB on core.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 5 Malignant

diagnoses.name: Malignant phyllodes tumour / primary sarcoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Malignant spindle cell neoplasm (malignant phyllodes tumour vs sarcoma vs metaplastic carcinoma).
diagnoses.comment: Core biopsy/excision with IHC required.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 5 Malignant

diagnoses.name: Angiosarcoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Malignant vascular neoplasm, suggestive of angiosarcoma.
diagnoses.comment: Bloody aspirate with atypical spindle/epithelioid cells; CD31/ERG on core; history of radiotherapy relevant.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 5 Malignant

diagnoses.name: Lymphoma of breast
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
diagnoses.comment: Flow cytometry/IHC; BIA-ALCL (CD30+, ALK−) in implant seroma.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 5 Malignant

diagnoses.name: Metastatic tumour to breast (melanoma, lung, ovary, etc.)
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Metastatic [type].
diagnoses.comment: IHC and clinical history needed.
diagnoses.cat: Category: IAC Yokohama System – 5 Malignant

extra.title: Triple test
items: Clinical + imaging + cytology. Concordant benign → follow-up; any discordance → core biopsy/excision.
Malignant FNA with concordant clinical/imaging can support treatment planning, but most centres still obtain core biopsy for receptors.

references: Field AS, Raymond WA, Schmitt F (eds). The International Academy of Cytology Yokohama System for Reporting Breast Fine Needle Aspiration Biopsy Cytopathology. Springer, 2020.
Field AS, Raymond WA, Rickard M, et al. The International Academy of Cytology Yokohama System for Reporting Breast Fine-Needle Aspiration Biopsy Cytopathology. Acta Cytol. 2019;63(4):257–273.
WHO Classification of Tumours Editorial Board. Breast Tumours. 5th ed. IARC, 2019.

systems.name: The Sydney System for Performance, Classification and Reporting of Lymph Node Cytopathology
systems.specimen: Lymph node FNA (palpation/US/EUS/EBUS), with ROSE and ancillary studies
use: Superficial and deep lymph node FNA in adults and children.
Can be combined with site-specific systems (e.g. thyroid Tg washout) for metastatic disease.
not_use: Extranodal lymphoid masses at other sites can use descriptive reporting (or WHO LN/spleen/thymus system).
Not a substitute for histology in primary lymphoma subtyping.
report_structure: Site, guidance, number of passes, ROSE
Ancillary tests performed (flow, IHC, FISH, molecular, microbiology)

adequacy.title: Performance & adequacy
items: Sydney part I covers performance: 22–27G needles, US guidance, ROSE, dedicated passes for flow cytometry (RPMI), cell block, microbiology (culture/CBNAAT) and molecular studies.
No numerical threshold; adequacy = sufficient representative, well-preserved material to answer the clinical question.
Necrotic material should prompt further passes from the periphery.

categories.name: Inadequate / Non-diagnostic
categories.definition: Insufficient, poorly preserved or obscured material, or material not representative of the lesion.

rom.source: Sydney system, Acta Cytol 2020;64:306
Meta-analysis, 9 studies/13,205 cases (Acta Cytol 2024;68:13, doi 10.1159/000535797) – pooled (95% CI)
Cancer Cytopathol 2024 review (doi 10.1002/cncy.22890) – range; average

categories.management: Repeat FNA (ultrasound-guided, with ROSE) or core/excision biopsy depending on clinical suspicion.
criteria: Scant lymphoid cells/blood only; crush or air-drying artefact; necrosis only without viable cells (necrosis alone can be informative).
Material not representative of the clinically/radiologically suspicious node.

diagnoses.name: Inadequate – scant/blood only
diagnoses.final: L1: Inadequate/non-diagnostic. Insufficient lymphoid material for evaluation.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat ultrasound-guided FNA with ROSE or biopsy recommended if clinically indicated.
diagnoses.cat: Category: Sydney System L1

diagnoses.name: Non-diagnostic – necrotic material only
diagnoses.final: L1: Non-diagnostic. Necrotic material only, no viable cells.
diagnoses.comment: Differential includes tuberculosis, necrotic metastasis and lymphoma. Suggest AFB stain/CBNAAT and repeat FNA from the viable periphery or biopsy.
diagnoses.cat: Category: Sydney System L1

categories.name: Benign
categories.definition: Reactive/benign lymphoid process with polymorphous population, or specific benign diagnosis.

rom.source: Sydney system, Acta Cytol 2020;64:306
Meta-analysis, 9 studies/13,205 cases (Acta Cytol 2024;68:13, doi 10.1159/000535797) – pooled (95% CI)
Cancer Cytopathol 2024 review (doi 10.1002/cncy.22890) – range; average

categories.management: Clinical follow-up; re-evaluate (repeat FNA/biopsy) if node persists or enlarges. Ancillary flow may support benign.
criteria: Polymorphous lymphoid population: small lymphocytes predominate with centrocytes, centroblasts, immunoblasts, plasma cells, tingible-body macrophages, lymphohistiocytic aggregates.
Specific benign patterns: granulomatous, suppurative, histiocytic, infectious.

diagnoses.name: Reactive lymphoid hyperplasia
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Reactive lymphoid hyperplasia.
diagnoses.comment: Polymorphous lymphoid population with tingible-body macrophages. Clinical follow-up recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Category: Sydney System L2

diagnoses.name: Granulomatous lymphadenitis
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Granulomatous lymphadenitis.
diagnoses.comment: Epithelioid granulomas ± multinucleated giant cells. Suggest ZN stain, CBNAAT/culture; differential sarcoidosis, fungal infection, cat-scratch disease.
diagnoses.cat: Category: Sydney System L2

diagnoses.name: Necrotizing granulomatous lymphadenitis consistent with tuberculosis
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Necrotizing granulomatous lymphadenitis, consistent with tuberculosis (AFB positive/negative).
diagnoses.comment: Caseous necrosis with epithelioid granulomas. ZN stain/CBNAAT result: [ ]. Correlate clinically.
diagnoses.cat: Category: Sydney System L2

diagnoses.name: Suppurative/acute lymphadenitis (abscess)
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Acute suppurative lymphadenitis.
diagnoses.comment: Neutrophils and necrotic debris; culture recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Category: Sydney System L2

diagnoses.name: Histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis (Kikuchi–Fujimoto)
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Features consistent with histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis (Kikuchi–Fujimoto).
diagnoses.comment: Karyorrhectic debris, crescentic histiocytes and plasmacytoid dendritic cells without neutrophils; exclude SLE.
diagnoses.cat: Category: Sydney System L2

diagnoses.name: Rosai–Dorfman disease
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Features consistent with Rosai–Dorfman disease.
diagnoses.comment: Large histiocytes with emperipolesis; S100+, CD68/CD163+, OCT2+, CD1a−.
diagnoses.cat: Category: Sydney System L2

diagnoses.name: Dermatopathic lymphadenopathy
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Reactive lymphadenopathy with dermatopathic features.
diagnoses.comment: Langerhans cells/histiocytes with melanin pigment; correlate with skin disease; exclude mycosis fungoides if suspected.
diagnoses.cat: Category: Sydney System L2

diagnoses.name: Infectious mononucleosis / viral lymphadenitis
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Reactive lymphoid hyperplasia with immunoblastic proliferation, compatible with viral (e.g. EBV) lymphadenitis.
diagnoses.comment: Monospot/EBV serology recommended; immunoblasts can mimic lymphoma.
diagnoses.cat: Category: Sydney System L2

diagnoses.name: Toxoplasma lymphadenitis
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Reactive lymphadenitis with microgranulomas (small epithelioid clusters), compatible with toxoplasmosis.
diagnoses.comment: Toxoplasma serology recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Category: Sydney System L2

diagnoses.name: Sarcoidosis
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Non-necrotizing granulomatous lymphadenitis; sarcoidosis is a consideration after exclusion of infection.
diagnoses.comment: Exclude tuberculosis and fungal infection (ZN/GMS stains, CBNAAT, culture); correlate with serum ACE, calcium and imaging.
diagnoses.cat: Category: Sydney System L2

diagnoses.name: Fungal lymphadenitis (histoplasma, cryptococcus)
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. Granulomatous lymphadenitis with fungal organisms (specify).
diagnoses.comment: GMS/PAS stains, culture.
diagnoses.cat: Category: Sydney System L2

diagnoses.name: Benign non-lymphoid (branchial cleft cyst, lipoma) – sampled as 'node'
diagnoses.final: L2: Benign. [Specify, e.g. contents of branchial cleft cyst].
diagnoses.comment: Squamous cyst in adults >40 years: exclude cystic metastatic HPV-associated SCC (p16/HPV testing).
diagnoses.cat: Category: Sydney System L2

categories.name: Atypical (cells of undetermined significance / atypical lymphoid cells of uncertain significance)
categories.definition: Atypical cells (lymphoid or non-lymphoid) insufficient for suspicious; or limited material/ancillary tests not available.

rom.source: Sydney system, Acta Cytol 2020;64:306
Meta-analysis, 9 studies/13,205 cases (Acta Cytol 2024;68:13, doi 10.1159/000535797) – pooled (95% CI)
Cancer Cytopathol 2024 review (doi 10.1002/cncy.22890) – range; average

categories.management: Repeat FNA with flow cytometry/cell block, or core/excision biopsy.
criteria: Predominantly small lymphocytes with a minor atypical population; possible low-grade lymphoma (e.g. follicular, MZL) but not confirmed.
Mixed population with increased large cells or atypical large cells; Hodgkin-like cells too few.
Few atypical non-lymphoid cells (carcinoma/melanoma not confirmed).

diagnoses.comment: Discohesive atypical lymphoid cells with lymphoglandular bodies, often angiocentric; hold steroids if possible and send fresh tissue for flow cytometry.
diagnoses.cat: Suggested template category: Lesional – diagnosis

diagnoses.name: Pituitary adenoma (PitNET)
diagnoses.final: Monotonous plasmacytoid cells – PitNET.
diagnoses.comment: Monotonous round cells with salt-and-pepper chromatin, loss of normal acinar mix; transcription-factor IHC on permanent sections.
diagnoses.cat: Suggested template category: Lesional – diagnosis

diagnoses.name: Schwannoma
diagnoses.final: Spindle cells – schwannoma.
diagnoses.comment: Cohesive fascicles of wavy spindle cells, Verocay-like palisades; S100/SOX10 confirm; vestibular location typical.
diagnoses.cat: Suggested template category: Lesional – diagnosis

diagnoses.name: Candida oesophagitis
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy; Candida present.
diagnoses.comment: Pseudohyphae with yeasts among squamous cells; correlate with endoscopic white plaques; may coexist with reactive atypia.

diagnoses.name: HSV/CMV oesophagitis
diagnoses.final: Viral cytopathic effect present.
diagnoses.comment: HSV: multinucleation, moulding, margination in squamous cells; CMV: large cells with owl-eye intranuclear inclusions in glandular/stromal cells. Usually immunocompromised; confirm by IHC/PCR.
